TI The Science Teacher Employability Scale for Private Schools: A
   Multidimensional Measure of Professional, Hiring, and Retention
   Competencies
SO HACETTEPE UNIVERSITESI EGITIM FAKULTESI DERGISI-HACETTEPE UNIVERSITY
   JOURNAL OF EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Teacher employability; Science education; Private schools; Scale
   development; Employability competencies
ID PSYCHOLOGICAL-ASSESSMENT; GRADUATE EMPLOYABILITY; HIGHER-EDUCATION;
   CONSTRUCT; VALIDITY
AB This study aimed to develop and validate the Science Teacher Employability Scale for Private Schools, a psychometric instrument designed to assess the employability levels of science teachers in the private sector. The study adopted a quantitative research paradigm and utilized a survey method. For the Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) during the initial development phase, the sample comprised 360 volunteer science teachers and pre-service teachers selected through random sampling. A subsequent sample of 200 science teachers and pre-service teachers participated in the Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA). The initial data collection instrument was a 56-item competency scale. To establish the scale's validity, comprehensive content, face, and construct validity assessments were conducted. Expert opinions were sought to confirm content and face validity, while both EFA and CFA were performed to rigorously examine construct validity. The scale's reliability was determined by calculating Cronbach's Alpha and composite reliability coefficients. As a result of the EFA, 23 items were removed, yielding a three-factor structure for the scale, which was subsequently confirmed by the CFA. The CFA results indicated an acceptable model fit, with a Root Mean Square Error of Approximation (RMSEA) of 0.08, a Goodness of Fit Index (GFI) of 0.96, a Comparative Fit Index (CFI) of 0.98, and an Incremental Fit Index (IFI) of 0.98. The overall Cronbach's Alpha coefficient for the final scale was a high 0.97, and the composite reliability coefficients for each sub-dimension approached or exceeded the 0.70 threshold. Consequently, this research has successfully developed a 33-item, three-dimensional scale that provides robust evidence of validity and reliability for assessing the employability of science teachers in private school settings. This instrument offers a valuable resource for recruitment, professional development, and research in the fields of teacher education and employment.

TI Perceptions of Classroom Teachers and Classroom Teacher Candidates
   Regarding the Türkiye Century Education Model
SO HACETTEPE UNIVERSITESI EGITIM FAKULTESI DERGISI-HACETTEPE UNIVERSITY
   JOURNAL OF EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE T & uuml;rkiye Century Education Model; classroom teacher; content
   analysis; perception; teacher candidate
AB The purpose of this study was to examine the perceptions of classroom teachers and classroom teacher candidates regarding the T & uuml;rkiye Century Education Model (TCEM) and to reveal the insights these perceptions offer about the model's applicability. The research was designed using the phenomenological (qualitative) method, one of the qualitative research designs. Participants consisted of 18 first-grade teachers working in various primary schools in the province of Van and 18 classroom teacher candidates studying at a public university. The participants were selected through criterion sampling, and data were collected using a structured interview form. The data were analyzed using content analysis. According to the research findings, teachers and teacher candidates generally evaluated TCEM positively as a student-centered, value-oriented model that prioritizes holistic development. The model's virtue-value-action approach, which targets not only academic success but also moral and social development, was considered a strong aspect. However, significant structural challenges emerge in the implementation of the model, including teacher competency, lack of technological infrastructure, overcrowded classrooms, inequalities in rural areas, and inconsistencies with the current exam system. In the study, it was also stated by the teacher candidates that since TCEM is still new, they were not adequately prepared for this model in education faculties, and they lacked confidence in whether the model would be long-lasting. Participants stated that for TCEM to succeed, multidimensional support should be provided, especially in the form of in-service training, mentoring programs, infrastructure investments, and flexible curriculum designs. Additionally, it was recommended that pilot implementations be expanded, teacher education systems be aligned with TCEM, and parent-community collaboration be strengthened.

   and Career Decidedness

   JOURNAL OF EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Digital generation; artificial intelligence anxiety; artificial
   intelligence literacy; career decidedness; mediating role
ID ARTIFICIAL-INTELLIGENCE
AB The main purpose in conducting this study is to investigate whether artificial intelligence anxiety has a mediating role in the effect of career decidedness on artificial intelligence literacy. This cross-sectional study, in which the correlational and predictive model was used, is noteworthy because it is probably the first study in the literature in terms of the scales used in it and the model developed. The study was conducted with 512 university students of the digital generation. Data were collected using the Artificial Intelligence Anxiety Scale, Artificial Intelligence Literacy Scale, and Career Decidedness Scale. SPSS and Jamovi software programs were used in the analysis of the data. The participating students obtained high mean scores from the Artificial Intelligence Literacy Scale, and Career Decidedness Scale, and a moderate mean score from the Artificial Intelligence Anxiety Scale. The results of the correlation analysis revealed that there was a negative and significant relationship between the scores obtained from the Artificial Intelligence Literacy Scale and Artificial Intelligence Anxiety Scale, a positive and significant relationship between the scores obtained from the Artificial Intelligence Literacy Scale and Career Decidedness Scale and a negative and significant relationship between the scores obtained from the Artificial Intelligence Anxiety Scale and Career Decidedness Scale. According to the results of the study, career decidedness had a direct and significant effect on artificial intelligence literacy, and artificial intelligence anxiety did have a partial mediating role in this relationship.

TI A Cross-Linguistic Cognitive Analysis of 'Nurturing a Potential
   Betrayer' Idioms and Implications for Idiom Teaching
SO HACETTEPE UNIVERSITESI EGITIM FAKULTESI DERGISI-HACETTEPE UNIVERSITY
   JOURNAL OF EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE idiom pedagogy; cognitive idiom analysis; contrastive phraseology; idiom
   equivalence; betrayal idioms
ID CONCEPTUAL METAPHOR; MENTAL-IMAGERY
AB This cross-linguistic cognitive study analyses nine "nurturing a potential betrayer" idioms across eight languages-English, Vietnamese, Chinese, French, Spanish, Arabic, Japanese, and Turkish-while addressing their pedagogical implications for language teaching and learning. Despite their shared cautionary function, idioms such as English to feed a snake in one's bosom and Vietnamese nu & ocirc;i ong tay & aacute;o ("to raise bees in one's sleeve") reveal unique conceptual metaphors and cultural frames. Utilizing source domains like SNAKE, BEE, CROW, TIGER, and DOG and the CONTAINER image schema, the nine idioms frame a disappointing betrayal by an intimate as the betrayer's inherent evil, a violation of reciprocity, or the nurturer's strategic failure. This challenges the notion of cross-linguistic idiomatic synonymy and highlights the risks of conceptual "false equivalents" in equivalence-based pedagogy. To address these issues, our research supports a cognitive-cultural approach for idiom analysis that highlights metaphor, imagery, and cultural contextualization, and proposes various teaching techniques such as visualization, scenario-based discussions, and contrastive mapping to enhance comprehension, retention, and pragmatic competence. Thus, idiom learning becomes an engaging exploration of cross-cultural meaning, based on each idiom's unique micro-model within the universal macro-model of The Danger of Nurturing a Betrayer.

TI Children's Gender Differences and Gender Stereotypes in the Context of
   Play
SO HACETTEPE UNIVERSITESI EGITIM FAKULTESI DERGISI-HACETTEPE UNIVERSITY
   JOURNAL OF EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Play; Gender differences; Gender stereotypes; Preschoolers; Early
   childhood
ID COGNITIVE THEORIES; GIRLS; BOYS; TOY; ROLES; EXPERIENCES; PREFERENCES;
   CHILDHOOD; RIGIDITY; PARENTS
AB Gender is a significant social construct in early childhood, significantly impacting children's play, peer interactions, and meaning-making processes. Utilizing a phenomenological qualitative framework, this study investigates preschool children's lived experiences of play and their processes of meaning-making concerning gender differences and stereotypes in play. The study included 64 children aged five and six and used semistructured interviews to collect data regarding their descriptions of play, toy preferences, choices of playmates, rules, and perceived consequences of rule violations. It is employed inductive content analysis to examine the data and identify shared units of meaning and variations in the children's lived experiences. The findings indicate that children of all genders generally perceive play as an enjoyable and social endeavor. But kids' accounts about the kinds of play, their favorite toys, their favorite friends, and how they understood violating the rules became more centered on gender. Children's narratives demonstrated gender biases, particularly when referring to toys and plays as "for girls" or "for boys." Girls typically expressed more flexible and inclusive interpretations of cross-gender plays, while boys' narratives demonstrated more rigid gender distinctions. Children's understanding of play rules and their consequences revealed gender-based stereotypes reflected in their perceptions of social interactions, authority, and exclusion during play. The results illustrate how crucial it is to create early learning settings that don't follow strict gender stereotypes and foster play that is open-ended and welcoming to everyone.

   Disabilities: A Training-Based Intervention

LA English
DT Article
DE Digital technologies; Digital security; Digital inclusion; Students with
   disabilities
ID INTELLECTUAL DISABILITIES; INTERNET USE; VICTIMIZATION; INDIVIDUALS;
   ACCESS; PEOPLE; YOUTH
AB This study, designed as a quasi-experimental single-group pretest-posttest model, examines changes in knowledge levels associated with an educational intervention designed to enhance the knowledge levels of university students with physical and sensory disabilities regarding the safe use of digital information and communication tools. Within the scope of the research, 15 students with disabilities were included in workshops on topics such as online dangers, digital literacy, digital addiction, cybercrime and methods of combating them. In the quantitative data collection process of this application, the data were obtained by pretest, post-test and retention test forms. According to the data obtained, the average of the pre-test applied to determine the level of knowledge of the participants about the safe use of digital information and communication technologies is 3.14; the average of the posttest is 4.40; the average of the permanence test is 4.02. To examine whether digital security knowledge changed significantly over time, a Friedman test was conducted comparing pretest, posttest, and retention test scores for the entire sample (N=15). The results indicated a statistically significant effect of time on participants' knowledge levels (chi(2)(2)=24.60, p<0.001). Post hoc Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Bonferroni correction showed that posttest and retention test scores were significantly higher than pretest scores (p<0.01), while the difference between posttest and retention test scores was not statistically significant (p>0.05), indicating that the knowledge gains were largely retained over time. The findings reveal that the training was associated with a statistically significant increase in knowledge levels of knowledge of the participants about digital security and that this improvement was sustained to a certain extent level. As a result, the study draws attention to the risks faced by people with disabilities in digital environments and emphasizes the importance of educational support for them to cope with these risks.

TI Sustainability and English Teachers' Professional Development Needs in
   the Era of Türkiye Century Education Model
SO HACETTEPE UNIVERSITESI EGITIM FAKULTESI DERGISI-HACETTEPE UNIVERSITY
   JOURNAL OF EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Education for sustainable development; environmental literacy;
   sustainability; English language teachers; curriculum
ID BOUND DIFFERENCES; STUDENTS
AB The T & uuml;rkiye Century Education Model, the recent curriculum reform, positions sustainability literacy as an explicit goal of English language learning and expects teachers to integrate sustainability-related themes and competencies into ELT (English Language Teaching) classrooms. However, sustainability is often treated as the responsibility of other subject areas; thus, there is limited evidence on whether English teachers possess the sustainability-related competencies and receive professional support needed to meet the curricular expectations. Addressing this gap, the present study investigated English teachers' sustainability-related competencies through the lens of environmental literacy and examined how teachers understand ESD, integrate sustainability into ELT and articulate their professional development needs. Using an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design, an online Environmental Literacy Questionnaire was administered to 372 English teachers, followed by semi-structured interviews with 12 participants. The quantitative results indicated broadly positive orientations toward sustainability and sustainability integration into ELT. However, participants demonstrated only moderate environmental knowledge and engagement in environmental behaviors, with routine low-cost actions reported more frequently than civic or collective forms of participation. Qualitative findings converged with these patterns. Most teachers supported sustainability integration in principle but reported limited familiarity with ESD and tended to address sustainability mainly when coursebooks thematized it. Only a small minority described sustained integration, typically under more flexible school conditions. Overall, the findings suggest that successful implementation of sustainability will require systematic, practice-oriented professional training that strengthens conceptual understanding of ESD/SDGs, models ELT-appropriate pedagogies, and supports materials adaptation within curricular constraints.

TI Vocabulary Development and Use of Cultural Language Elements in Fourth
   Grade Elementary School Students

LA English
DT Article
DE Turkish language teaching; national identity; cultural language
   elements; vocabulary; forms of expression
AB One of the important aims of education is to transmit culture and values. This study aims to examine the vocabulary, use of cultural language elements, and narrative styles of fourth-grade primary school pupils. Among the general objectives of Turkish national education is to foster a sense of national identity and instill Turkish culture, with the aim of raising citizens who embrace, preserve, and develop cultural values and love their country and nation. This study examined and determined the extent to which this objective was achieved among fourth-grade primary school students. Cultural language activities encompass the Turkish way of life, associated ideas and national values. Therefore, including cultural language activities in the teaching and learning process is expected to contribute positively to students' internalization of the structure of the Turkish language and their development of national identity. This study utilized qualitative research methods. The research design was a basic qualitative design. Semi-structured interview forms and compositions were used in this study. The study group consisted of 58 pupils attending the fourth grade of primary school. It can be said that the implementation of cultural language activity education contributed to the pupils' use of cultural language elements and the formation of national identity awareness. It was determined that students used epic narrative forms when describing their love for the flag and literary art when describing their love for their homeland. This research makes recommendations regarding the inclusion of in-class and out-of-class activities that will foster cultural acceptance and national identity awareness in line with learning outcomes.

TI Teaching Interactional Strategies in an Online L2 Turkish Classroom: A
   CA-Informed Five-Step Model for Turn-Taking and Floor Management*

   JOURNAL OF EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Action research; Turkish as a second language; synchronous online
   instruction; interactional strategies; turn-taking; discourse markers
ID CONVERSATION ANALYSIS; ORGANIZATION
AB This study examines how interactional strategies and awareness of spoken language can be introduced, developed, and practiced in a synchronous online Turkish as a second language (TSL) setting through a conversation analysis (CA)-informed pedagogical framework. Employing an action research design, the study implemented iterative instructional cycles with five adult L2 Turkish learners in live Zoom-based classes. Drawing on qualitative data from classroom interaction, learner reflections, and task-based speaking performances, the study proposes and evaluates a five-step teaching model consisting of (1) feedback, (2) preparation and awareness-raising, (3) watching and conversation analysis, (4) in-class speaking tasks, and (5) out-of-class speaking tasks. The findings suggest that this model may support learners' emerging interactional competence, as reflected in more frequent participation, greater use of discourse markers, and an increased orientation to turn-taking and floor management. Learners also reported heightened awareness of differences between spoken and written Turkish, along with reduced speaking anxiety and enhanced communicative self-confidence. Overall, the study indicates that CA-informed, interaction-focused online instruction may be a productive approach to fostering interactional competence within this cohort when pedagogical design emphasizes sustained, socially situated interaction.

TI Evaluation of Criminal Responsibility in Terms of Discipline and
   Criminal Law in the Neurobiological and Genetic Causes of Violence
   Behaviors in Children and Adolescents*
SO HACETTEPE UNIVERSITESI EGITIM FAKULTESI DERGISI-HACETTEPE UNIVERSITY
   JOURNAL OF EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Child neuro-law; violence; crime; criminal liability
ID AGGRESSION; PREVENTION
AB Many factors can be effective in the violent behavior of children and adolescents. The aim of this study is to contribute to the evaluation and prevention of criminal behavior by examining the neurological, biological, hormonal and genetic dimensions of violent and aggressive behaviors seen in children and adolescents. Another aim is to examine studies that support the evaluation of criminal responsibility in children's criminal behavior from a neuro-legal perspective. Another aim of the study is to draw attention to the differences between disciplinary and criminal law in the assessment of children's criminal responsibility. Adolescence is generally a challenging period of life. During this period, many processes such as conscious thinking, decisionmaking, foreseeing the consequences of actions, impulse control, planning, problem solving, continuity, consistency, behavioral control, and risk assessment are possible with the full maturation of the frontal lobe and prefrontal cortex. Delays in the development of the frontal lobe and lesions in the prefrontal cortex can lead to negative emotional reactions and violent behavior. Violent antisocial behavior and high levels of impulsivity are often associated with the prefrontal lobe region of the brain. Studies have shown that antisocial and criminal individuals have structural and functional abnormalities in the prefrontal cortex, temporal cortex, insula, amygdala and hippocampus. For these reasons, evaluations and regulations regarding criminal responsibility in adolescents' criminal behavior need to be reconsidered. Taking into account the latest developments regarding brain structure and genetics will contribute to the assessment of criminal responsibility of children and adolescents who commit crimes and to the healthy functioning of the juvenile justice system.

AB The purpose of this research was to analyze the efficacy of the Fun Easy Learn app in enhancing seventh-graders' command of the Arabic lexicon (mufradat). The study used a one-group pretest-posttest design, which is a quasi-experimental approach. There were 27 participants, drawn at random from a pool of 100 pupils. Vocabulary tests were given both before and after the therapy to gather data. The three topics addressed by the instruments were animals, jobs, and body parts. The data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics in SPSS version 31.0. At a significance threshold of 0.000 (p < 0.05), the paired-samples t-test yielded a t-value of-6.819, indicating a statistically significant difference between the pretest and posttest scores. Based on these results, it's clear that the Fun Easy Learn app helps students learn Arabic words faster. Students were more invested, enthusiastic, and motivated to study Arabic because of the app's interactive elements, including images, audio pronunciation, and educational activities. We may conclude that the Fun Easy Learn app is a useful tool for madrasah students to increase their Arabic vocabulary.

The study concludes that future curriculum models must be based on an integrated system that responds to scientific and technological challenges without neglecting the socio-cultural values of native speakers.

TI Nonlinear association between the composite dietary antioxidant index
   and kidney stone disease: Mediation by systemic immune-inflammatory
   status in a cross-sectional study
SO SCIENCE PROGRESS
LA English
DT Article
DE composite dietary antioxidant index; kidney stones; statistical
   mediation; inflammation; cross-sectional study
ID TEMPORAL TRENDS; RISK; CALCIUM; HEALTH; PREVALENCE; INSIGHTS; ZINC; MEN
AB Objective Oxidative stress and inflammation have been implicated in kidney stone disease. The Composite Dietary Antioxidant Index (CDAI) reflects the combined intake of multiple dietary antioxidants, but its association with kidney stones and the potential statistical contribution of immune-inflammatory markers remain unclear. This study aimed to examine the association between CDAI and kidney stones and to explore the potential statistical contribution of systemic immune-inflammatory markers to this association.Methods This was a retrospective cross-sectional study of adults aged >= 18 years. We analyzed data from 26,485 participants in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2007-2018. Survey-weighted logistic regression was used to examine the association between CDAI and self-reported history of kidney stones. Restricted cubic spline analyses were performed to assess nonlinear associations, and subgroup, sensitivity, and exploratory mediation analyses were conducted.Results After full adjustment for potential confounders, higher CDAI was inversely associated with kidney stones (OR = 0.97, 95% CI: 0.96-0.99). When CDAI was categorized into quartiles (Q1-Q4), participants in the highest CDAI quartile had 22% lower odds of kidney stones compared with Q1 (OR = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.66, 0.93). Restricted cubic spline analysis suggested a nonlinear inverse association that tended to plateau at higher CDAI levels. Furthermore, exploratory mediation analyses suggested statistical indirect associations through the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), with indirect association proportions of 3.11%, 5.27%, and 3.14%, respectively. The advanced lung inflammation index (ALI) showed no significant indirect association.Conclusions In this nationally representative cross-sectional study, higher CDAI was inversely associated with kidney stones. Exploratory mediation analyses suggested statistical indirect associations through immune-inflammatory markers. These findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in prospective studies.

TI Development of an automatic approaching trigger measurement system based
   on macro-micro collaborative motion
SO SCIENCE PROGRESS
LA English
DT Article
DE macro-micro stages; approaching; secondary triggering; high-precision;
   system
ID PRECISION
AB To solve the contradiction between the large-stroke motion of the stage and high-precision measurement, a Fast Automatic Approaching Trigger Measurement System (FAATMS) based on macro-micro cooperative motion is proposed herein. This system effectively combines a large-stroke macrostage (LSMS) and a six-degree-of-freedom microstage (6-DOFMS). A three-dimension (3D) motion control and nanoscale triggering method was adopted, involving the rapid movement of the LSMS and the cooperation of the 6-DOFMS for secondary triggering. Before measurement, the LSMS drives the sample to approach the probe quickly to realize a coarse triggering. After the first triggering is completed, the program is automatically switched to enter the 6-DOFMS control to achieve the second precise triggering. The 3D LSMS has a stroke of more than 100 mm & times; 100 mm & times; 100 mm. The designed 6-DOFMS is driven by hybrid series and parallel piezoelectric ceramic actuators. The interior adopts a hollow design and is used to install the stage for placing the measured sample, which can be effectively combined with the LSMS to achieve high-precision measurement tasks. The 3D displacement of the FAATMS is measured by laser interferometers. The three-axis laser beams converge on the probe and comply with the Abbe principle throughout the entire measurement range. Based on the secondary triggering strategy of the collaborative motion control of the macro-micro stages, the system drives the sample to trigger the probe ten times in each of the five directions of X+, X-, Y+, Y-, and Z. The peak-to-peak (PP) value of the repeatability measurements was 64.9 nm, and the standard deviation was less than 39.1 nm (k=2). By conducting precise measurements at the micro-nano level on the standard sphere, with a diameter repeatability of 330 nm (k=2), demonstrating the reliability and accuracy of this automatic approaching trigger method in practical applications can be re-evaluated. A series of experimental results show that the developed FAATMS is of great significance for improving the fundamental manufacturing technology and can provide a reference for precision measurement and high-end equipment manufacturing.

TI Low-temperature plasma adenoidectomy versus conservative treatment for
   children with adenoid hypertrophy and allergic rhinitis: A
   non-randomized observational study
SO SCIENCE PROGRESS
LA English
DT Article
DE low-temperature plasma; adenoid hypertrophy; allergic rhinitis;
   children; adenoidectomy
ID IMPROVEMENT
AB Objective: To investigate the effect of low-temperature radiofrequency ablation (LTRFA) adenoidectomy on the improvement of allergic rhinitis (AR) in children with adenoid hypertrophy (AH) complicated by AR, in comparison with conservative pharmacological management. Methods: A total of 89 pediatric patients with AH complicated by AR were enrolled in this non-randomized observational study. Among them, 59 underwent LTRFA adenoidectomy under nasal endoscopy, and 30 received conservative anti-allergic therapy (patients who declined surgical intervention). Symptom severity was assessed using the visual analog scale (VAS; score 1-10) at baseline and at 6 months of follow-up. Improvement was defined as a reduction in VAS score of >= 3 points from baseline. Between-group comparison of VAS change scores was performed using an independent-samples t-test. Results: Baseline VAS scores were comparable between groups (surgical: 7.85 +/- 1.46; conservative: 7.63 +/- 1.52; P=0.512). At 6 months, the mean VAS change score was 4.95 +/- 1.90 in the surgical group and 2.51 +/- 1.44 in the conservative group, a difference that was statistically significant (P<0.001). Based on the improvement criterion (VAS reduction >= 3 points), 52 of 59 surgical patients (88.1%) and 17 of 30 conservative patients (56.7%) met the threshold (chi(2)=11.30, P<0.001). Conclusions: In children with AH complicated by AR, LTRFA adenoidectomy was associated with significantly greater improvement in nasal symptom scores at 6 months compared with conservative treatment. These findings suggest that LTRFA adenoidectomy may be a beneficial treatment option; however, given the non-randomized design and limited follow-up duration, further randomized controlled trials with objective outcome measures are needed to confirm these preliminary observations.

TI An improved deep learning-based MSA-Net model for small liver tumor
   segmentation
SO SCIENCE PROGRESS
LA English
DT Article
DE computer-aided diagnosis (CAD); small tumor segmentation;
   representation; image segmentation; U-Net; MSA-net; multi-scale
   convolutions; attention-based mechanism
ID NEURAL-NETWORK
AB Objective Liver cancer is one of the most fatal types of cancer in the world, and early identification is one of the most crucial considerations that may improve the likelihood of recovery. Hence, building a computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) system that improves radiologists' operations by providing automated, high-precision small-tumor segmentation in complicated medical imaging is the main objective of this research study.Methods Conventional deep learning techniques, like U-Net, have shown impressive overall tumor delineation results, but they frequently struggle to distinguish between large and small tumors. The occurrence of tiny tumors and tumors with different shapes in the intricate liver exacerbates this deficiency. This paper proposed an MSA-Net (Multi-Scale Attention Network), a variant of the U-Net architecture, to address these problems. This is accomplished by the effective extraction of small-tumor features, which is made possible by the architecture's integration of multi-scale convolutional layers into the encoder and decoder pathways, as well as an attention mechanism that concentrates on salient regions and gathers contextual data across several receptive fields.Results The proposed MSA-Net was trained and tested using the publicly accessible 3DIRCADb and LiTS datasets. The 3Dircadb dataset yielded a dice score of 92.00% and a Jaccard index of 86.00% for small tumors, whereas the LiTS dataset yielded a dice score of 72.57% and a Jaccard index of 65.35% for small tumors.Conclusion In contrast to other research, our technique assesses the outcomes by evaluating large and small tumors independently. The findings demonstrate that MSA-Net greatly improves segmentation, particularly in tiny tumors, demonstrating its usefulness in real-world clinical contexts.

TI Exploring empathic strategy use in interactive dialogue applications: A
   latent profile and discourse analytic study
SO TURKISH JOURNAL OF EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Dialogue interactions; Empathic strategies; Latent profile analysis
ID NUMBER
AB This study investigates empathic strategy use in interactive dialogue practices and examines how these patterns emerge across distinct profile levels. Grounded in an explanatory sequential mixed methods design, the research conceptualizes empathy not as a fixed personality trait but as a context-sensitive, interactionally constructed resource. In the quantitative phase, data collected from 350 undergraduates across multiple universities were analyzed using Latent Profile Analysis (LPA), yielding four empathic strategy use profiles: high-level, balanced, selective, and low-level. These profiles reflect not only differences in usage intensity but also divergent interactional orientations. In the qualitative phase, dialogues from structured interaction tasks encompassing problem-solving, negotiation, and emotionally loaded contexts were analyzed through interactional discourse analysis. Findings indicate that high-level profile students deploy empathic strategies to sustain interaction and foster mutual understanding, whereas low-level profile students demonstrate markedly limited interactional engagement. Balanced and selective profiles exhibited context-sensitive and strategically regulated empathic responses. Collectively, the results suggest that empathic strategies constitute a dynamic and functionally significant component of interactive dialogue competence.

AB This study examined the impact of parental involvement on adolescent athletes' dual career competency and the mediating role of motivational dimensions based on Self-Determination Theory. Using a quantitative cross-sectional design, data were collected from 489 licensed athletes aged 12-18 years participating in individual and team sports in Rize, T & uuml;rkiye. Participants completed measures of parental involvement, sport motivation, and dual career competency. TI University students' digital literacy skills, attitudes to social media
   use, and social media addictions
SO CONTEMPORARY EDUCATIONAL TECHNOLOGY
LA English
DT Article
DE digital literacy; social media addiction; student attitudes; technology
   use; digital behavior
ID COMPETENCE; SCALE
AB This study aims to examine the relationship between university students' digital literacy skills, their levels of social media addiction, and their attitudes toward social media use. A quantitative research method was employed, utilizing a correlational survey design. The sample included a total of 412 students from three different universities who responded to online forms. Data were collected using three standardized measurement tools in addition to a participant information form: the Bergen social media addiction scale, the social media attitude scale, and the digital literacy scale. The data were analyzed using SPSS and the adapted PROCESS macro version 4.2. Independent samples t-test, analysis of variance, Pearson correlation analysis, and moderation analysis were conducted. The findings reveal that students' positive attitudes toward social media may increase their levels of social media addiction, whereas higher levels of digital literacy appear to reduce addiction. Furthermore, it was determined that social media attitude positively affects digital literacy, and digital literacy has a suppressive effect on social media addiction. Analyses based on gender, academic year, and field of study indicate that male students exhibit higher levels of digital literacy and more positive attitudes toward social media; engineering students demonstrate greater competence in digital skills; and digital literacy improves significantly as academic level increases. In this regard, it is recommended that university administrations implement educational programs aimed at enhancing digital literacy and develop supportive interventions, particularly for first-year and social sciences students. Promoting content that encourages students to use social media in a more conscious, productive, and critical manner may be beneficial for both reducing addiction and increasing digital competence. Additionally, future research should support quantitative findings with qualitative data, replicate studies across different cultural contexts, and incorporate current variables related to the use of technological tools into the model.

TI Modeling AI Tool Adoption in Higher Education: The Role of Authentic
   Learning and Prompting Competence
SO ELECTRONIC JOURNAL OF E-LEARNING
LA English
DT Article
DE Artificial intelligence in higher education; Technology acceptance
   model; Authentic learning; Prompt engineering competence; Behavioral
   intention
ID TECHNOLOGY; STRATEGIES
AB As AI tools are increasingly used in higher education, understanding the factors affecting students' adoption intentions has become theoretically and practically important. Previous studies have mainly relied on traditional technology acceptance constructs, while comparatively little attention has been given to pedagogical and competence-based conditions shaping students' cognitive evaluations of AI systems. To address this gap, the current study builds on the technology acceptance model (TAM) by proposing authentic learning (AL) and prompt engineering competence (PEC) as precursors of perceived usefulness (PU), perceived ease of use (PEU), and behavioral intention (BI) to use AI tools. The study was based on data collected from 309 undergraduate students at the University of Ha'il. A two-step structural equation modeling (SEM) approach was employed using AMOS software. Confirmatory factor analysis confirmed construct reliability, convergent validity, and discriminant validity. SEM was then conducted to test the hypotheses. The findings show that AL significantly predicts both PU and PEU, whereas PEC significantly predicts PEU but not PU. Both PU and PEU were found to be important predictors of BI. Bootstrapping results reveal that AL affects BI through PU and PEU, while PEC affects BI entirely through PEU. The results also confirm considerable explanatory power, with an R2 of .71 for BI. These findings extend TAM by reconceptualizing AL as a foundational pedagogical precursor influencing AI adoption and by clarifying the unique role of PEC in improving PEU. Integrating pedagogical and competence-based determinants into AI-enabled higher education advances technology acceptance theory and explains the AI adoption mechanism more precisely. The findings provide practical guidance for educators and instructional designers by emphasizing the importance of integrating authentic learning tasks and developing students' prompt engineering skills to enhance meaningful AI-supported learning.

TI Biographical Portraits of Ukrainian Educators: Reconstruction of the
   Pedagogical Heritage (Second Half of The 19th Century - Beginning of The
   21st Century)
SO ESPACIO TIEMPO Y EDUCACION
LA English
DT Article
DE History of Education; Educational Heritage; Biographical Research;
   Collective Biography; Digital Humanities; Politics of Memory
ID COLLECTIVE BIOGRAPHY; HISTORY
AB This article examines the Encyclopaedic Dictionary "Pedagogues of Ukraine (Second Half of the 19th-Early21st Century)" as a scholarly project aimed at reconstructing and systematising national pedagogical heritage that was fragmented as a result of political repression, forced migration, and long-term ideological pressure. The purpose of the study is to substantiate the significance of collective biographical research for the restoration of educational memory and the reintroduction of marginalised figures into the history of education. The research is based on a qualitative methodological framework that combines historical-pedagogical analysis, biographical and prosopographical approaches, and principles of source criticism. Particular attention is given to the criteria for selecting biographical entries, the representativeness of the corpus, and the contextual interpretation of individual pedagogical trajectories. The source base includes materials of the Encyclopaedic Pedagogical Biographical Dictionary, archival documents, pedagogical publications, memoirs, periodicals, and selected multimedia sources related to the lives and professional activities of Ukrainian educators of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. The study demonstrates that collective biography enables a comprehensive understanding of pedagogical processes that cannot be fully captured through individual life histories alone. It allows for the identification of shared professional patterns, intellectual networks, and the impact of political and cultural contexts on educational thought. The article concludes that the Encyclopaedic Dictionary "Pedagogues of Ukraine (Second Half of the 19th-Early 21st Century)" functions as an effective scholarly tool for preserving educational heritage, supporting the politics of memory, and integrating Ukrainian pedagogical experience into broader international research in the history of education.

DT Article
DE Healthcare personnel; hospitals; organizational justice; quality of
   life; task performance
ID SCALE
AB BACKGROUND: Role-based performance in an organization's workforce is essential to its sustainability. Hence, this study aimed to examine the mediating role of organizational justice in the quality of work-life and role-based performance among hospital employees. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional design was adopted, and the research data were gathered from Adventist hospitals in Southwestern Nigeria using a multistage sampling technique in 2024. A sample of 303 employees responded to the research questionnaire, which included the quality of work-life scale, role-based performance scale, and organizational justice scale. The Sobel test result indicated that organizational justice indeed mediated the relationship between work-life quality and role-based performance (Z = 2.35, SE =.05, P < .05). CONCLUSION: The study concluded that excellent quality of work-life and organizational justice result in increased role-based performance and productivity.

The purposes of this research were to study the factors predicting and development of a care model for dependent among the elderly. After the intervention, the mean QoL score significantly increased from 2.89 to 4.56 (t = -7.43, P < 0.001). Cronbach's alpha coefficient equal to 0.86, 0.85, and 0.90, respectively. The care model consists of six components: preliminary screening, health promotion and disease prevention, health care, health recovery, family relationships, and community participation. Satisfaction with the care model and its implementation was reported at the highest level. CONCLUSION:The strengthening community-based resources and social support networks to ensure sustainable care. These community factors are crucial for advancing early prevention, timely intervention, and meeting the health care needs of an increasingly aging society. The model's success lies in the integration of health assemblies and participatory action, providing a scalable framework for rural elderly care policy.

AB BACKGROUND:Patient safety is an important aspect of healthcare system. Owingto improper training, there is high mortality and morbidity involved in patient care in hospitals worldwide. This study aimed to analyze the patient safety culture awareness among healthcare professionals in India. MATERIALS AND METHODS:This prospective cross-sectional study was conducted in different hospital settings following Institutional ethical Committee approval. Hospital survey on patient safety culture developed by Agency Healthcare Research Quality professionals was used which comprised of thirty questions grouped in 11 dimensions including supervisor's/managerial expectations, actions promoting patient safety, organizational learning, continued improvement and hospital teamwork. Statistical analysis: The Pilot study was conducted using the SPSS Statistical tool software version 20.0 (IBM, NY) for testing the reliability of the questionnaire by usingthe Cronbach alpha test. The calculated sample size was found to be 100 for performing the pilot study. Cronbach alpha score of 0.734 was obtained which was indicative of study validity. Responses were recorded on 5-point Likert scale, i.e., 1 = strongly disagree, 2 = disagree, 3 = neither agree nor disagree, 4 = agree, and 5 = strongly agree). The Chi-square test/goodness of fittest was usedfor determination of statistical significance of qualitative variables, while Chi-square and Mann-Whitney Utests were used for intergroup comparisons. P < 0.05 was considered to have statistical significance. RESULTS:The 'hands off' and transitions domain required demonstrated lower positive responses (35.56%). Higher positive responses were obtained from dimensions: teamwork within a unit (92.21%), organizational learning and continued improvement (89.49%), frequency of reported events (82.31%), and feedback and communication errors (69.19%). Least positive responses were obtained from two dimensions-(a) general perception (20.23%) and (b) nonpunitive response to errors (09.12%). On comparison between perception responses by use of'Chi-square' test, statistically significant difference (<0.05) was obtained between following variables-(a) perception regarding patient safety dimensions and position and (b) experience level of healthcare professionals. CONCLUSION:There is requirement of improvement in few domains to strengthen patient safety culture in India which can be done by means of training programs in hospitals.

TI Examine the effects of the developed Pender's model constructs on
   medication compliance and adherence to a low-salt diet in patients with
   uncontrolled hypertension
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Diet; hypertension; low sodium diet; medication adherence; Pender's
   health promotion model
ID BLOOD-PRESSURE; HEALTH; BEHAVIORS; EFFICACY
AB BACKGROUND: One of the challenges for patients with high blood pressure is the lack of proper control. The aim of this study was to investigate the influence of the developed Pender's model structures on medication compliance and adherence to a low-salt diet in patients with uncontrolled hypertension in the city of Ahvaz. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted among patients with uncontrolled blood pressure in Ahvaz city. The participants were selected through multistage sampling. The data collection instrument was a researcher-designed questionnaire based on the constructs of the developed Pender's model, which included three sections with demographic information, questions about adherence to a healthy and low-salt diet, and medication adherence. The data were analyzed using PLS SMART software. RESULTS: The results of the study revealed that the constructs self-efficacy (path coefficient = 0.25, P < 0.00), perceived sensitivity (path coefficient = 0.17, P < 0.02), and interpersonal influences (path coefficient = 0.09, P < 0.02) had a positive and significant influence on adherence to a low-salt diet, and the structure of perceived benefits (path coefficient = -0.09, P < 0.00) had a negative and reverse effect on this behavior. Additionally, the results of the study revealed that the self-efficacy construct (path coefficient = 0.11, P < 0.02) had a positive and significant effect on medication adherence, and the perceived barrier construct (path coefficient = -0.13, P < 0.00) had a negative and reverse effect on this behavior. CONCLUSION: By adding perceived sensitivity to the Pender's health promotion model, there is the possibility of better control of hypertension in patients with uncontrolled blood pressure.

TI Effectiveness of computer game-based rehabilitation protocol on the
   health-related quality of life and glycosylated hemoglobin in elderly
   diabetics
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Diabetes mellitus; dual-task performance; exergaming; glycated
   hemoglobin (HbA1c); quality of life (QOL); type 2
ID OLDER-ADULTS
AB BACKGROUND:Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is one of the greatest challenges in healthcare today and is evolving into a pandemic, due to significant comorbidity and mortality. Physical activity (PA) plays a crucial role for older adults by preventing or delaying functional and psychological decline from aging and comorbidities like diabetes, while also positively impacting their health-related quality of life (HR-QOL). Exergaming serves as an emerging form of exercise that combines technology, games, and leisure. Hence, this study determines the impact of computer game-based rehabilitation protocol (CGRP) on HR-QOL and glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c) values in elderly diabetics. MATERIALS AND METHODS:A single-blinded randomized controlled trial (RCT) was conducted on 82 participants allocated into two groups (41each). Group A (control) received a conventional physiotherapy program, while Group B (experimental) underwent CGRP. Outcome measures, including HbA1c levels and HR-QOL, were assessed at baseline and after 12 weeks of rehabilitation. Within-group changes in HbA1c and World Health Organization Quality of Life Brief Version (WHOQOL-BREF) domain scores were evaluated using paired t-tests, while between-group differences were analyzed with independent t-tests. A P-value less than or equal to 0.05 was considered statistically significant. RESULTS:Significant reduction in HbA1c levels was observed in the experimental group (P < 0.00001) after the intervention, and a notable shift from poor to good diabetes control status was observed. Additionally, the QOL scores improved significantly in the experimental group (P < 0.00001). CONCLUSION:The current study demonstrated that CGRP is an effective intervention for improving glycemic control and HR-QOL in elderly individuals with T2DM. The dual-task nature of CGRP, which combines PA with cognitive engagement through interactive games, appears to offer a unique advantage over conventional interventions.

TI School-based mental health promotion and behavioral modification in
   pubertal adolescents: A controlled intervention study
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Behavioral modification; puberty; school based mental health program;
   school students
ID METAANALYSIS
AB BACKGROUND:Adolescence represents a period of rapid physical, emotional, and cognitive transition. Early pubertal changes, hormonal fluctuations, and psychosocial pressures increase vulnerability to behavioral disturbances. School-based mental health programs have been shown to enhance coping ability, emotional regulation, and adaptive behavior among adolescents. To evaluate the effect of a school-based mental health program on behavioral modifications during puberty among school students in Bhubaneswar. MATERIALS AND METHODS:A quasi-experimental pre-test post-test control group design was adopted among 92 adolescents aged 9-15 years selected through purposive sampling. A socio-demographic proforma and a 30-item Behavioral Modification Scale were used. The experimental group received a structured five-session mental health program; the control group received no intervention. Behavior was significantly associated with age, gender, pubertal stage, educational level, and family type. CONCLUSION:The school-based mental health program effectively improved behavioral modification among early adolescents. Findings highlight the necessity of integrating structured mental health education into school curricula.

TI Improving knowledge of iron deficiency anemia through a nurse-led
   educational program: A Quasi-experimental study among adolescent girls
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Adolescent; anemia: iron-deficiency; female; health education; health
   promotion; knowledge; Quasi-experimental studies; schools; students
AB BACKGROUND: In India, iron deficiency anemia remains common among adolescent girls, with low awareness persisting despite school-based programs. In this context, we conducted a study to assess their knowledge and evaluate the effectiveness of a structured health promotion program on iron deficiency anemia among adolescent girls in a school. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The study was conducted among 136 girls aged 12-15 years across 7th, 8th, and 9th standard students selected without randomization. Participants attended a one-hour interactive health education session developed by the researchers, using video aids and lectures. Pre- and post-test assessments measured knowledge gains using a structured, validated questionnaire developed by the researchers. Outcomes were compared within participants using their own pre-intervention scores as the comparator, consistent with a quasi-experimental single-cohort design. All eligible students who were present on the day of the intervention and assessments were included. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, paired t-tests, Cohen's d, and multivariable linear regression to explore predictors of improvement. RESULTS: Among 7th standard students, mean scores increased from 6.23 to 13.34 (P < 0.001), followed by 8th standard (6.96 to 12.90, P < 0.001) and the 9th standard (7.82 to 10.45, P < 0.001) using R software. Multivariable regression further showed that lower income and younger grade level were associated with higher post-test gains. CONCLUSION: Targeted, interactive school-based interventions can play a critical role in addressing persistent knowledge gaps on iron deficiency anemia among adolescent girls. In this study, a single nurse-led educational session produced significant improvements in knowledge, with the largest gains observed in younger students and those from lower-income households. These findings underscore the importance of tailoring health promotion content to the age, baseline understanding, and socioeconomic background of the learners. By leveraging their clinical expertise, community presence, and communication skills, nurses are uniquely positioned to deliver such context-specific interventions, bridging knowledge gaps early and fostering healthier behaviors that can help reduce the long-term burden of anemia.

TI Academic burnout and the protective role of self-efficacy among sports
   science undergraduates in Indonesia: A cross-sectional study
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Burnout; cross-sectional studies; health promotion; Indonesia;
   psychological; self-efficacy; students; universities
AB BACKGROUND: Academic burnout disproportionately affects sports science undergraduates facing dual academic-athletic stressors, with self-efficacy attenuating vulnerability. This study examined the association between self-efficacy and academic burnout and quantified burnout odds across self-efficacy strata in Indonesia. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted from March to May 2025 among 233 junior-year sports science undergraduates (semesters 3 and 4) at State University of Makassar, South Sulawesi, Indonesia. Participants were selected using simple random sampling, with a response rate of 83.2%. Ethical clearance was granted by the university's biomedical research ethics board. Academic burnout was measured using the Indonesian-validated MBI-SS (15 items; Cronbach's alpha = 0.87), while self-efficacy was assessed using the Indonesian-validated GSES-12 (12 items; Cronbach's alpha = 0.83). Data analysis employed Spearman's correlation and binary logistic regression using IBM SPSS Statistics version 24.0, with statistical significance defined as P < 0.05. RESULTS: Participants exhibited predominantly moderate self-efficacy (70.4%), with 49.8% demonstrating moderate burnout and no severe cases. Spearman analysis revealed a significant negative association (rho = -0.172, 95% CI [-0.297, -0.038], P = 0.008). Binary logistic regression confirmed each one-level increase in self-efficacy reduced burnout odds by 53.6% (OR = 0.464, 95% CI [0.261, 0.823], P = 0.009; Nagelkerke R2 = 0.040). Predicted probabilities were 72.7%, 55.2%, and 36.4% for low, moderate, and high self-efficacy, respectively. CONCLUSION: Self-efficacy was significantly and inversely associated with academic burnout among Indonesian sports science undergraduates, with clinically interpretable predicted probability benchmarks supporting tiered health promotion interventions for burnout prevention in sports science education.

TI Combined counseling based on the Fogg behavior model for managing weight
   gain in pregnant women: A randomized controlled trial protocol
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Behavioral intervention; Fogg behavior model; gestational weight gain;
   mobile health; pregnancy; randomized controlled trial
AB Appropriate weight gain during pregnancy is essential, as inappropriate weight gain (too much or too little) has complications for both mother and baby, and the ideal amount depends on the mother's body mass index. Balanced nutrition and exercise are the main foundations of a healthy pregnancy, and counseling during this period is an opportunity to promote maternal and fetal health and reduce risks such as preterm birth, gestational diabetes, and hypertension caused by excessive weight gain. This study aims to evaluate the effect of a combined counseling intervention program based on the fogg behavioral model using mobile phone technology (whatsapp or eta) on total gestational weight gain and perinatal outcomes. A randomized controlled trial in qom, iran, will recruit pregnant women to develop a whatsapp platform for individualized, continuous pregnancy weight management services based on the fogg behavior model. All participants will be included in the full analysis set (fas), while the per-protocol set (pps) will consist of women who completed the intervention and provided all outcome data. This study highlights the effectiveness of consultations utilizing the fogg model in managing appropriate weight gain during pregnancy. If the findings confirm that the fogg model-based counseling promotes healthy weight gain in pregnant women, this approach could be implemented during pregnancy to effectively minimize instances of excessive or inadequate weight gain to significantly reduce cases of excessive or insufficient weight gain.

TI Effectiveness of a comprehensive therapeutic milieu on quality of life
   and level of stress among patients with heart failure - An experimental
   study
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Heart failure; Quality of life; Stress level; Comprehensive therapeutic
   milieu
ID SELF-CARE; INTERVENTIONS; DEPRESSION; IMPACT; ASSOCIATION; MANAGEMENT;
   ANXIETY
AB BACKGROUND:Heart failure (HF) is a chronic and progressive condition associated with significant physical limitations, psychological distress, and impaired quality of life (QoL). Despite advances in medical management, many patients continue to experience persistent symptoms and elevated stress levels. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of a comprehensive therapeutic milieu on QoL and stress level among patients with HF. MATERIALS AND METHODS:A true experimental pretest-posttest control group design was used. The sample size (n = 240) was calculated based on 80% power, a 5% level of significance, and a medium effect size (Cohen's d = 0.5). Participants were allocated to study and control groups using stratified randomization based on age and gender. The intervention group received a 90-day comprehensive therapeutic milieu, while the control group received routine care. RESULTS:At pretest, most participants in both groups reported poor QoL and moderate stress levels. By posttest, the study group demonstrated significant improvement in the physical dimension, emotional dimension, and overall QoL compared to the control group (P < 0.001). The mean stress score in the study group decreased from 23.28 +/- 3.85 at baseline to 16.57 +/- 4.22 at posttest III, whereas the control group showed minimal change. A moderate positive correlation was observed between stress and QoL scores (r = 0.571 in the study group; r = 0.658 in the control group, P < 0.001), indicating that increased stress is associated with poorer QoL as higher scores on both scales represent worse outcomes. CONCLUSION:The study finding concluded that integrating structured psychosocial support and low-intensity physical activity into routine cardiac care may enhance holistic management and improve long-term patient outcomes.

TI Effect of immersive virtual reality on pain and anxiety during lumbar
   puncture: A randomized controlled trial
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Anxiety; lumbar puncture; meningitis; pain management; virtual reality
ID VISUAL ANALOG; RELIABILITY; VALIDITY; PROGRAM
AB BACKGROUND: Lumbar puncture (LP) is a commonly performed diagnostic procedure essential for cerebrospinal fluid analysis in neurological conditions. LP is frequently associated with pain and anxiety, which may negatively affect patient cooperation and procedural outcomes. The study aimed to evaluate the effects of virtual reality (VR) in reducing pain and anxiety during LP procedure. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A randomized controlled trial was conducted at two tertiary teaching hospitals in Iraq. 85 candidates for LP were randomly assigned to intervention (41) and control groups (44) from May to October 2025. Data were collected by Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) and VAS for Anxiety. Before the LP procedure, participants in the intervention group were given a 15-min VR session. At predetermined intervals, such as baseline (before to intervention) and right after the LP, outcome assessments were carried out. Primary outcome pain intensity measured immediately after lumbar puncture. Secondary outcomes: Anxiety level measured at baseline, 15 min prior to LP and immediately after the procedure. Pain intensity measured at additional time points (baseline and pre-procedure) for comparison. Data were entered into the SPSS version 26.0 and analyzed using Kolmogorov-Smirnov Test, Mann-Whitney U tests, Levene's test, Wilcoxon Signed Ranks Test and Spearman's rank correlation coefficient at a significance level of P <= 0.001. The outcome assessors and data analysis was blinding in the study. RESULTS: Pain severity measured immediately after LP was significantly lower in the VR group compared to the control group. The mean pain score in the VR group was 2.49 +/- 0.675, whereas it was 8.36 +/- 1.348 in the control group. The mean difference between groups was -5.87 (95% confidence interval [CI]: -6.32 to -5.42), indicating a statistically and clinically significant reduction in pain in favor of the VR intervention (r = 0.610; P = 0.001). While, anxiety statistically significant reduction after VR exposure (6.11, 95% CI 5.48-6.74). Conversely, the control group's post-test scores continued to be considerably higher than those of the VR group, and there was no discernible decrease in pain or anxiety over time (P > 0.05). Between-group comparisons confirmed significantly lower post-intervention pain and anxiety scores in the VR group (P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Immersion VR may be a useful non-pharmacological strategy for reducing procedural discomfort and anxiety in individuals having LPs, according to the results of this randomized controlled experiment. However, these findings should be regarded as preliminary due to the methodological constraints of the study, such as sample size and single-setting design. To validate these results and determine the wider application of VR in clinical practice, more extensive, multi-center research is advised.

TI A randomized controlled trial comparing the efficacy of art therapy and
   mindfulness on depression, anxiety, and stress among elderly people
   living in old age homes in Salem district, Tamil Nadu
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Aged; anxiety; art therapy; depression; homes for the aged; mindfulness;
   stress
AB BACKGROUND: The mental health burden (depression, stress, anxiety) is significant among institutionalized elderly. The interventions, such as art therapy and mindfulness, have gained importance in managing common mental health disorders. This three-arm parallel randomized controlled trial (RCT) aimed to assess the efficacy of art therapy and mindfulness intervention among the elderly. MATERIALS AND METHODS:A three-arm, parallel-group RCT was conducted in six selected old age homes. Study sites were selected using the probability proportional to size sampling method to ensure a representative sample. A total of 240 elderly residents aged 60 and over were recruited using simple random sampling through the lottery method. The participants were then randomly divided into three groups: two intervention groups (combining art therapy and mindfulness) and a control group (CG) that received routine activities of daily living. The baseline assessment (T0) was carried out before the intervention, and the post intervention assessment (T1) was carried out after the end of the intervention period. The Depression, Anxiety and Stress Scale-21 was used as a standardized instrument to measure the outcome variables. RESULTS: All the 240 participants were divided equally and randomly allocated to the predetermined groups. The mean and standard deviation of age were found to be 72.10 +/- 9.74 years. Post intervention, the participants in "extremely severe" category were reduced from 36 (15%) to 28 (11.7%) in depression, 116 (48.3%) to 97 (40.4%) in anxiety, and 2 (0.8%) to 1 (0.4%) in stress. After the intervention, art therapy showed significant within-group reductions in depression, anxiety, and stress. Compared to the CG, both art therapy and mindfulness showed significant reductions in depression, anxiety, and stress (P < 0.01). Between-group comparisons indicated that art therapy led to better outcomes than mindfulness for anxiety and stress, while no statistically significant differences were observed for depression. CONCLUSION: The combined art therapy and mindfulness program is a demonstrated short-term effectiveness, scalable intervention for improving the mental well-being of institutionalized older adults. These interventions can be integrated into elderly mental health care to enhance the emotional well-being of the elderly.

TI The ultrasound wave enhanced carbon nanotube encapsulated dacarbazine
   effect on melanoma cell death via ER stress-mediated apoptosis

AB BACKGROUND:In this study regarding the unique properties of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) to improve drug solubility, stability, and cellular uptake, combined with the mechanical effects of ultrasound wave, we aimed to elucidate how this synergistic approach influences cell death through endoplasmic reticulum stress (ER stress)-mediated apoptosis. TI Assessment of knowledge and attitudes of pregnant women toward
   pregnancy-related risk factors in Mosul City, Iraq
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Antenatal care pregnancy; attitudes; knowledge; maternal health; risk
   factors
AB BACKGROUND: Reducing negative pregnancy outcomes depends on maternal knowledge of pregnancy-related risk factors. Developing efficient maternal health interventions in post-conflict Mosul, Iraq, where the healthcare system has been significantly compromised, will depend on assessing pregnant women's knowledge and attitudes regarding pregnancy risks. This study sought to evaluate knowledge and attitudes about pregnancy-related risk factors among pregnant women in Mosul City, Iraq, as well as to identify the socio-demographic factors influencing this knowledge. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted from January to April 2024 in Mosul City, Iraq. From January to April 2024, 420 pregnant women attending antenatal clinics in Mosul participated. Socio-demographic information was gathered using a standardized questionnaire; knowledge and attitudes regarding pregnancy risk factors were also evaluated using this tool. Knowledge scores were calculated and analyzed in relation to demographic variables using appropriate statistical tests. RESULTS: The mean knowledge score was 15.63 +/- 5.72 out of a possible 30 points, indicating moderate knowledge levels. Only 23.8% of participants demonstrated good knowledge. Higher knowledge scores were significantly associated with higher education level (P < 0.001), urban residence (P = 0.003), higher income (P = 0.001), and receiving antenatal care in private facilities (P = 0.002). Most women recognized risks associated with hypertension (76.4%) and diabetes (72.9%), but fewer recognized the significance of fetal movement changes (42.3%) and vaginal bleeding (53.1%). While 87.3% of participants had positive attitudes toward seeking medical care for complications, 47.6% held misconceptions about culturally rooted risk factors, such as dietary taboos and traditional remedies. CONCLUSION: Pregnant women in Mosul demonstrated moderate knowledge of pregnancy-related risk factors with significant educational and socioeconomic disparities.

TI Effectiveness of web-based application for dental health promotion among
   elementary school teachers: A randomized controlled trial
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Dental health promotion; teacher; web application
ID ORAL-HEALTH
AB Dental caries in elementary school children can be prevented through dental health education and promotion in schools. Teachers play an important role in supporting children's oral health behaviors. The use of web-based applications as a health promotion medium is expected to improve the effectiveness of dental health education by providing easier access and broader reach. This study aimed to assess the effectiveness of a web-based application in improving teachers' knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding dental health promotion among elementary school children. This randomized controlled trial (RCT) employed a pretest-posttest control group design involving 120 primary school teachers in Aceh Province, Indonesia, who were randomly assigned to intervention and control groups. The intervention group demonstrated significantly greater improvements in knowledge, attitudes, and practices than the control group (P < 0.05), with progressive increases observed from the pretest to both post-intervention assessments. The findings indicate that the web-based application is effective in improving teachers' knowledge, attitudes, and practices related to dental health promotion in elementary schools.

TI Comparative evaluation of gut health, inflammatory factors, and sleep
   quality among shift workers: A cross-sectional study
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Circadian rhythm; inflammation; intestinal permeability; shift work;
   sleep
ID BRAIN AXIS; MICROBIOTA
AB BACKGROUND: Night-shift work disrupts the body's natural circadian rhythm, leading to impaired sleep quality, altered gut function, and reduced emotional well-being. Circadian misalignment affects sleep duration and efficiency, disturbs gastrointestinal (GI) regulation, and increases the risk of mood disorders such as anxiety and depression. These cumulative effects can significantly impact overall health and quality of life in shift workers. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional comparative study was conducted among 200 individuals (100 day-shift and 100 night-shift workers) aged 25-40 years at a tertiary care hospital in Pune. Data was obtained using a structured questionnaire designed to assess sleep, gastrointestinal symptoms, and emotional health. Blood samples were analyzed for lipopolysaccharide (LPS), zonulin, C-reactive protein (CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha). Data was analyzed using SPSS version 25.0 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA); significance was set at P < 0.05. RESULTS: Night-shift workers reported significantly more gastrointestinal issues (heartburn, bloating, constipation, indigestion; P < 0.050) and emotional distress (P = 0.010) compared to day-shift workers. Elevated gut permeability markers (LPS: P = 0.003; zonulin: P = 0.005) were also found among night-shift workers. Inflammatory markers (CRP, IL-6, TNF-alpha) were significantly higher among night-shift workers (P < 0.010), indicating systemic inflammation. The quality of sleep was poor, along with shorter duration among night-shift workers, which was further aggravated by co-use, like smoking and alcohol (P = 0.004). Night-shift workers, especially the higher income group and females, experienced greater sleep disturbances and distress (P < 0.020). Day-shift workers who did regular physical exercise had improved sleep quality (P = 0.003). CONCLUSION: Night-shift work is associated with poor sleep quality, increased gut permeability, and elevated inflammatory markers in the body. Lifestyle interventions focusing on sleep, diet, and stress may reduce health risks associated with poor sleep quality.

TI Enhancing self-efficacy in nursing internship students through Reiki
   practices: A randomized controlled trial
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Complementary therapy; nursing education; nursing students
   self-efficacy; randomized controlled trial; therapeutic touch
ID EXERCISE; IMPACT
AB BACKGROUND: Self-efficacy is crucial for nursing students transitioning into clinical practice. Reiki, an energy therapy, shows promise in enhancing self-perception and well-being. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of Reiki practices on the self-efficacy of nursing internship students. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A single-blind randomized controlled trial was conducted at Mashhad University of Medical Sciences, Iran, from April to July 2023. Forty-four nursing internship students were randomly divided using sealed envelopes into either an intervention group (n = 22), who underwent Reiki Level I training and daily self-practice for 21 days, and a control group (n = 22), who received no intervention. Data were collected using a demographic information form and the General Self-Efficacy Questionnaire (GSE-10) before and after the intervention. Kolmogorov-Smirnov, Chi-square, independent t-tests, and paired t-tests were performed using SPSS 16, with significance set at P < 0.05. RESULTS: Both groups were demographically comparable at baseline. There was no statistically significant difference in self-efficacy scores between the intervention and control groups before the intervention (P = 0.468). However, after the intervention, the self-efficacy scores in the intervention group were significantly higher than those in the control group (P = 0.002). CONCLUSION: Reiki Level I training and practice significantly enhanced self-efficacy among nursing internship students, which suggests its potential as a complementary strategy in nursing education. Future research should explore the long-term impact and broader applications of Reiki in diverse educational and cultural contexts.

TI Audit and feedback to improve antibiotic prescribing among community
   physicians in India: A quasi-experimental study
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Antimicrobial stewardship; educational; feedback; intervention; primary
   health care; quasi-experimental studies
AB BACKGROUND: Irrational antibiotic use, especially in Indian community settings, is a major contributor to the growing global threat of antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Guidelines for rational prescribing are provided by the WHO AWaRe classification; however, its use in primary care is still restricted. An effective way to enhance prescribing practices is through audit and feedback. The purpose of this study was to assess community physicians' use of antibiotics, gauge their compliance with the AWaRe framework, and ascertain whether structured audit and feedback can encourage sensible prescribing and aid in the fight against AMR. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The study was conducted in two phases from July 2022 to 2023 in Chengalpattu, Tamil Nadu. Phase 1 involved a cross-sectional review of 680 antibiotic prescriptions. In Phase 2, 28 community physicians participated in a quasi-experimental study using a validated structured questionnaire. Educational intervention and feedback were provided. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 26.0, and the Wilcoxon signed-rank test was applied with a significance level of P < 0.05. RESULTS: Amoxicillin was the most commonly prescribed antibiotic (88.2%) out of 680 prescriptions, mostly for upper respiratory tract infections. While access-group medications like amoxicillin were more commonly used in rural areas, watch-group antibiotics like azithromycin were more frequently used in urban areas. Perception scores (19 to 16, P = 0.000) and knowledge (median: 26.5 to 20, P = 0.000) significantly improved after the audit and feedback intervention. Increased adherence to the WHO AWaRe classification was observed in post-intervention prescribing patterns, with a discernible shift towards community physicians' use of antibiotics sensibly, especially when treating acute respiratory infections. CONCLUSION: Enhancing antibiotic stewardship and encouraging rational prescribing among community physicians at the primary care level through audit and feedback is a practical and economical approach that can improve adherence to AWaRe classification and decrease inappropriate antibiotic use.
