TI Exploring the cycle: "Perceptions, perspectives, and practices of
   substance use in young adults"
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Adolescents; prevelance; rural; substance abuse; young adults
ID ABUSE
AB BACKGROUND: Substance abuse among adolescents and young people is a growing public health concern, with significant implications for both individuals and society. This study sought to investigate the Perceptions, Perspectives, and Practices (3Ps) related to substance use, as well as explore contextual factors influencing drug and alcohol engagement among youth in the Dehradun district of Uttarakhand, India.MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted in semi-urban and rural areas of Dehradun, screening 14,203 participants aged 10-24 years through multistage stratified random sampling. Data were collected using self-administered questionnaires, which included the standardized and locally-adapted CRAFT and ASSIST screening instruments. RESULTS: Among the 3290 participants with complete socio-demographic data, 77.0% of males and 41.5% of females reported a family history of drug abuse (P < 0.0001). About 85.4% of participants in the 20-24 age group reported such a history. Regarding perceptions, 70.8% identified cannabis as a highly addictive substance (n = 1959). Knowledge of side effects was limited: less than one-third recognized key physical harms (n = 1493). Analysis of attitudes (n = 3236) revealed that 30.1% to 34.8% believed some drugs like cannabis are not addictive, while 60.6% agreed that even first-time use can lead to addiction. Curiosity, peer pressure, and family history emerged as the most common reasons for initiation, especially among males. CONCLUSION: These findings emphasize the need for targeted educational interventions-particularly about long-term consequences-and for strengthening protective factors in families and peer groups. Systematic, context-aware prevention strategies are essential to reduce substance abuse and its health and social impact among young people in India.

TI Analysis of psychomotor latency, spatial reasoning, and metabolic health
   markers in adolescent gamers: A comparative study of the impact of the
   confounding triad of sleep, diet, and screen modality
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Adolescents; anthropometry; cognitive function; metabolic health;
   psychomotor performance; reaction time; screen time; sleep quality;
   video games
AB BACKGROUND:<br /> The purpose of this research is to understand the complex relationships of the intensity of electronic gaming and the neurocognitive (Reaction Time, IQ, Spatial IQ) and bodily (BMI, Skinfolds, Visual Acuity) components. Of particular interest was stating for the first time the novelty of the 'Confounding Triad' of sleep, food (caloric) gaming, and the specific screen type of the gaming interface.<br /> MATERIALS AND METHODS:<br /> A comparative cross-sectional study was carried out on a stratified random sample of 200 male adolescents (ages 13 to 21) from northern India. Participants were stratified into gamers (>= 5 hours/week, n = 122) and non-gamers (<5 hours/week, n = 78). The psychomotor speed was measured using a digital Audio-Visual Reaction Timer, IQ was measured using the Stanford-Binet Intelligence Scale, and Spatial Quotient via online standardized battery, while subcutaneous adiposity was measured using Harpenden skinfold calipers. The confounders were measured using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), a 24-hour dietary recall, and Non-Gaming Screen Time (NGST) logs. Mann-Whitney U tests were used for group comparisons, and Generalized Linear Models (GLM) and Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA) were used to determine independent effects.<br /> RESULTS: Compared to non-gamers, gamers displayed faster rates across Auditory, Visual, and Aim Reaction Times (P < 0.001) and better Spatial Quotient (P = 0.001). The GLM for Visual Reaction Time demonstrated a dose-dependent improvement for hours spent playing games (beta = -2.15, P < 0.001) that was present even when considering the negative effect on performance from poor sleep (beta = +4.35 per unit increase in PSQI, P < 0.001). Gaming status was significant for the ANCOVA for skinfold thickness (P = 0.035), but dietary caloric intake was the more important variable (eta 2 = 0.19, P < 0.001). No significant difference was found in IQ (P = 0.36) or in visual acuity.<br /> CONCLUSION: The findings indicate that regular practice of interactive gaming provides players with better cognitive and psychomotor skills, even when sleep deprivation is considered. With that said, dietary surplus imposes greater metabolic hazards than gaming behaviors. Therefore, health interventions are encouraged not only to regulate gaming hours but to prioritize the teaching of digital hygiene.

TI A randomized controlled clinical trial of the effect of positive
   psychology on childbearing Intention and Stages of behavior change in
   reproductive age women
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Childbearing; intention; positive psychology; transtheoretical model of
   behavior change
ID DECISION AID; KNOWLEDGE
AB BACKGROUND: In contemporary societies, delayed childbearing and declining fertility rates have emerged as prominent reproductive behavior patterns globally. This demographic shift has precipitated significant population aging trends, presenting substantial socioeconomic challenges. This study aimed to investigate the effect of positive counseling on childbearing intention and stages of behavior change among women. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study employed a two-arm randomized clinical controlled trial on married women unwilling to conceive within two years following marriage until the next two years. The exclusion criteria encompassed contraindications to pregnancy such as cardiovascular diseases, autoimmune disorders, severe psychiatric conditions, a history of hysterectomy, and similar factors. Initially, one-fifth of 88 health centers across various city districts were selected using simple random sampling to ensure socioeconomic diversity. Then, participants were recruited using convenience sampling method from 88 health centers. The participants were assigned into two groups (n = 27per group) with a ratio of 1:1 with block size of 6 using Random Allocation Sampling (RAS) software. The intervention group attended seven weekly group counseling based on positive psychology. The childbearing intention and stage of behavior change questionnaires were completed before and 4 weeks after the intervention. To compare the mean scores of outcomes, the ANCOVA statistical test was used. The Chi-square test was used for comparison of stages of behavior change in childbearing. RESULTS: The results indicated that after counseling, the overall mean score of childbearing intention [Adjusted Mean Difference (AMD): 8.58, 95% CI: (5.18-11.99), P < 0.001] significantly increased in the intervention group compared to the control group. A statistically significant difference was observed between the two groups in terms of the frequency of the stages of childbearing behavior change after the intervention (P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: This study provides empirical evidence supporting the integration of positive psychology-based counseling into public health interventions aimed at addressing declining fertility rates.

TI The association of dietary fiber, antioxidants, and micronutrients with
   metabolic syndrome among fishermen and farmers: The mediating role of
   physical activity (A case-control study)
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Dietary intake; farmers; fishermen; metabolic syndrome; physical
   activity
ID ZINC; RISK
AB BACKGROUND:Metabolic syndrome (MetS) considers as one of the public health problem due to increasing of MetS prevalence worldwide. Farmers and fishermen in Aceh Regency are groups that are risk of metabolic syndrome (MetS) due to unstable socio-economic conditions. This study aimed to identify dietary factors, including fiber, antioxidants, and micronutrients, associated with MetS among these populations. MATERIALS AND METHODS:A case-control study was conducted with 240 participants (120 cases with MetS and 120 controls without MetS) from Lhokseumawe and North Aceh. Biochemical components, including Fasting Blood Glucose (FBG) and lipid profile were performed by Regional Hospital Medical Team. Dietary intake was assessed using 2 & times; 24 hour food recall, and physical activity was measured using the International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ). Non-parametric independent t-test was used to analyze the difference of intake between groups, while characteristics of respondents were compared in two groups using chi square and fisher exact test. Linear and logistic regression were performed to conduct multivariate analysis and to analyze the mediating role of physical activity. RESULTS:The analysis revealed a higher intake of energy and lower micronutrient intake in the cases group (P < 0.05). Physical activity significantly mediated the association between certain dietary intakes (such as energy, vitamin C, and magnesium) and MetS (P < 0.05), while partial mediation was observed for zinc (P < 0.05). CONCLUSION:These findings highlight the importance of dietary improvements and increased physical activity in reducing MetS risk in fishermen and farmers in Aceh.

TI A pathway to health: Spiritual health and health-promoting behaviors in
   parents of children with ASD
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Autism spectrum disorder; health behavior; parents; spirituality
ID SPECTRUM DISORDERS; AUTISM
AB BACKGROUND:Caring for a child with ASD presents challenges for parents, affecting their health. Spiritual health can enhance health-promoting behaviors. This study examined the relationship between spiritual health and health-promoting behaviors in parents of children with ASD. MATERIALS AND METHODS:A cross-sectional study was conducted on 178 Iranian parents of children with ASD in 2024 using convenience sampling. Data were collected using demographic, spiritual health, and health-promoting lifestyle questionnaires. Descriptive statistics, independent t-test, one-way ANOVA, and Pearson correlation were used for analysis in SPSS22 with a statistical significance level set at P < 0.05. RESULTS:In this study, 46.6% of the parents were aged 30-40, and 89.9% of them were female. Doctors and health professionals (1.55) and the Internet (1.33) were the most common sources of health information for parents. The mean score of health-promoting behaviors for the parents of the study was 131.60 +/- 24.42. The mean spiritual health of the parents was 86.14 +/- 19.06. Spiritual health was low in 1.7% of the mothers, moderate in 71.3%, and high in 27%. CONCLUSION:This study found a significant relationship between spiritual health and health-promoting behaviors in parents of children with ASD. Parents with higher levels of spiritual health were more likely to engage in activities that support their overall health. However, a large number of parents report only a moderate level of spiritual health, which highlights the need for targeted interventions. Strategies such as spiritual counseling, spirituality-based programs, and support groups can help improve the spiritual health and health of these parents.

TI Enhanced corrosion resistance and electrochemical stability of hybrid
   HA-Cu-collagen nanocoatings on Ti-6Al-4V alloy in physiological
   environments
SO SCIENCE PROGRESS
LA English
DT Article
DE nanostructured coatings; electrochemical deposition process; Ti-6Al-4V
   alloy; calcium phosphates-copper-collagen; corrosion behavior
ID HYDROXYAPATITE COATINGS; BEHAVIOR
AB In this study, the corrosion behavior of hydroxyapatite (HA), hydroxyapatite-copper (HA-Cu), and hydroxyapatite-copper-collagen (HA-Cu-Col) nanocoatings electrochemically deposited on Ti-6Al-4V alloy was systematically investigated. For the hybrid coatings, collagen was incorporated via an immersion process followed by heat treatment at 80 degrees C for 1 hour. Grazing incidence X-ray diffraction (GIXRD) confirmed the retention of the HA phase across all coatings, with Cu addition leading to co-precipitation of metallic Cu phases, evidenced by distinct peaks at 2 theta angles of 34.3 degrees, 42 degrees, and 50.4 degrees. Collagen integration, without forming new phases, resulted in a uniform organic-inorganic matrix and enhanced nanoscale porosity. Field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM) revealed that the HA coating exhibited a dense needle-like morphology with lengths of 1-5 mu m and rod diameters of 200-500 nm, whereas HA-Cu displayed a granular-floret structure interspersed with 20-50 nm copper nanoparticles. The hybrid HA-Cu-Col coating formed a compact fibrous-floret network with nanoscale uniformity. Tafel polarization tests indicated the highest corrosion potential (Ecorr) for HA-Cu-Col at +0.54 V vs. Ag/AgCl reference electrode, while the lowest corrosion current density (Icorr) was achieved with HA at 0.027 & micro;A/cm2, followed by HA-Cu-Col at 0.040 & micro;A/cm2, confirming that the hybrid system maintains low corrosion kinetics while introducing stable passivation behavior. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy data after 48 hours of immersion showed coating resistances (Rcoat) of 2885, 13268, and 12851 Omega.cm2 for HA, HA-Cu, and HA-Cu-Col, respectively, whereas the highest charge transfer resistance (Rct) of 1078 k Omega.cm2 was observed for HA-Cu-Col, indicating superior suppression of interfacial electrochemical reactions despite the moderate Rcoat value at extended immersion. Overall, the hybrid HA-Cu-Col nanocoating exhibited enhanced impedance behavior, suggesting improved barrier properties through higher charge transfer resistance, stable passive region formation (0.64-1.58 V), controlled ionic diffusion, and bio-inspired networking. Although initial open-circuit potential (OCP) fluctuations point to interfacial dynamics that warrant further long-term investigation, the coating remains a promising candidate for Ti implant applications in physiological environments.

TI Associations between albumin-bilirubin score and all-cause mortality
   among individuals with acute myocardial infarction: A cohort study based
   upon MIMIC-IV
SO SCIENCE PROGRESS
LA English
DT Article
DE acute myocardial infarction; ALBI; all-cause mortality; MIMIC-IV
   database; critically ill populations
ID HEPATOCELLULAR-CARCINOMA; STATEMENT
AB Objective: The albumin-bilirubin (ALBI) score is a validated prognostic tool in liver diseases. Nevertheless, its role in acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains underexplored. This research sought to explore associations between ALBI score and all-cause mortality (ACM) among individuals with AMI. Methods: This retrospective cohort study used MIMIC-IV v3.1 data. Patients were classified into four groups by ALBI score quartiles. The primary outcomes encompassed ACM within 30 and 365 days. Kaplan-Meier (KM) curves were used to compare differences in survival outcomes among the four groups. Cox proportional hazards models were used to investigate associations between ALBI scores and ACM. Moreover, restricted cubic splines (RCS) were employed to investigate dose-response relationships between ALBI score and ACM at different time points among individuals with AMI. We calculated the area under the ROC curve (AUC), integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), and net reclassification improvement (NRI) to evaluate the incremental predictive value of adding ALBI to the SOFA, SAPSII, and APSIII scoring systems. Results: In total, 2,105 patients were included, 1,294(61.47%) were men. KM curves showed lower survival in highest vs lowest ALBI quartile((log-rank P<0.05) Cox proportional hazards regression analysis indicated that in the extensively adjusted model, when ALBI was analyzed as a continuous variable, each one-unit elevation correlated with a 47.7% rise in ACM within 30 days(adjusted HR=1.477, 95%CI:1.249-1.746, P<0.001) and a 52.2% rise in ACM within 365 days (adjusted HR=1.522, 95%CI:1.331-1.741, P<0.001).When ALBI was examined as a categorical variable, compared to the Q1 group, the risks of ACM in the Q4 group were 1.873 times higher within 30 days and 1.784 times higher within 365 days. RCS analyses indicated a positive linear association between ALBI score and ACM within 14, 30, 90, and 365 days. In addition, the inclusion of ALBI in the SOFA, SAPSII, and APSIII scoring systems enhanced the predictive accuracy of the models. Conclusions: High ALBI scores may be associated with an increased risk of ACM in critically ill patients with AMI admitted to ICUs, and ALBI may provide incremental prognostic information independent of conventional critical illness scoring systems.

TI Load state identification of rock bolts based on energy and multiscale
   permutation entropy of ultrasonic signals
SO SCIENCE PROGRESS
LA English
DT Article
DE rock bolt; piezoelectric active sensing; wavelet packet energy;
   multiscale permutation entropy; load state identification method
ID THERMAL PROTECTION PANELS; VIBROACOUSTIC MODULATION; CONTACT
AB Monitoring the load state of rock bolts is of great importance for ensuring the safe operation of geotechnical and underground structures. In view of the pronounced stage-dependent variation of ultrasonic response characteristics under complex contact interface conditions at the anchorage end, this study proposes a stage-wise identification method for rock bolt load states based on wave energy and multiscale permutation entropy (MPE). Starting from the mechanical evolution of the anchorage interface, wavelet packet energy is employed in the low-load stage to characterize the global response dominated by the average contact stiffness, while MPE is introduced in the high-load stage to capture the enhanced interface nonlinearity and the evolution of signal complexity. In this way, stable identification of the rock bolt load state over the entire loading range is achieved. To validate the proposed method, a multi-path piezoelectric (PZT) excitation-reception experimental system was established, and ultrasonic reflection signals were collected under different working conditions and loading levels. The experimental results indicate that wavelet packet energy exhibits high sensitivity to variations in bolt load during the low-load stage, whereas MPE shows a stable and monotonic evolution with increasing load in the high-load range. Owing to the complementary characteristics of the two features across different loading stages, the proposed stage-wise identification strategy enables full-range characterization of the rock bolt load state. The findings provide a physically interpretable ultrasonic monitoring approach for assessing the load state of rock bolts under complex contact interface conditions.

TI A mixed-methods study of patient grievances with phlebotomy services at
   a tertiary care hospital in eastern India
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Health services accessibility; hygiene; Likert scale; patient
   satisfaction; phlebotomy; tertiary care hospital
AB BACKGROUND:Patient satisfaction with phlebotomy services is an important indicator of healthcare quality and efficiency. It reflects not only clinical standards but also environmental and interpersonal dimensions of care. Understanding patient experiences can guide meaningful improvements in diagnostic service delivery, especially in high-volume public hospitals. The aim of this study was to assess patient satisfaction with phlebotomy services in a tertiary care hospital, identify critical factors influencing perceptions, and highlight specific areas requiring enhancement.MATERIALS AND METHODS:A sequential mixed-methods, cross-sectional survey was conducted among 100 patients visiting the phlebotomy section at All India Institute of Medical Sciences Gorakhpur, a tertiary care institute in eastern Uttar Pradesh, India. A 35-item structured questionnaire was administered in English or Hindi, according to participant preference. The tool included both closed-ended questions rated on a 3-point Likert scale and open-ended items capturing qualitative feedback. Quantitative data were analyzed using SPSS, and thematic analysis was applied to open-ended responses. Gender-specific patterns in satisfaction were also explored.RESULTS:High levels of satisfaction were reported for hygiene practices (96%-99%), staff professionalism (94%-96%), and information sharing (77%). The availability of required laboratory tests was positively rated by 79% of participants. However, areas of concern included long waiting times (28% dissatisfaction) and toilet cleanliness (18% dissatisfaction). Thematic analysis revealed that staff attitude, cleanliness, communication, and waiting time were dominant influences on patient satisfaction, whereas pain and procedural delays emerged as common grievances. Gender-based analysis revealed that female patients expressed higher satisfaction with staff behavior and communication, whereas male patients were more satisfied with procedural and diagnostic efficiency.CONCLUSION:The study not only found overall high patient satisfaction with phlebotomy services but also identified actionable gaps in waiting time management, sanitation, and communication. Targeted improvements in these areas, especially with gender-sensitive approaches, can further enhance the patient experience and align phlebotomy services with patient-centered care models in tertiary care settings.

TI A pilot study evaluating a low-cost virtual reality simulator for
   transesophageal echocardiography training in anesthesiology residents
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Anesthesiology/education; clinical competence; computer simulation;
   echocardiography; transesophageal/education; education; graduate;
   medical; pilot projects; virtual reality
ID SURGERY
AB BACKGROUND:Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) is an essential skill in perioperative and critical care practice. Traditional lecture-based instruction remains the standard for foundational training, but virtual reality (VR)-based platforms may enhance engagement and provide scalable, self-directed learning. This exploratory study evaluated the feasibility, educational impact, and learner satisfaction of a low-cost VR TEE training system for anesthesiology residents.MATERIALS AND METHODS:In this randomized, single-center study, 19 anesthesiology residents (Post-Graduate Years 1-3) without prior TEE experience were assigned to lecture instruction or VR-based training. Participants completed baseline, immediate post-training, 1-month, and 3-month knowledge assessments evaluating TEE principles and clinical correlation. A post-training survey assessed satisfaction and perceived educational value.RESULTS:Both groups showed improvement in knowledge scores with retention at 1 and 3 months. There were no significant differences in mean scores between groups (control vs. VR: baseline 14.4 +/- 3.6 vs. 14.9 +/- 4.2, P = 0.779; postintervention 15.4 +/- 6.1 vs. 16.5 +/- 4.2, P = 0.670; 1-month 16.0 +/- 6.5 vs. 16.8 +/- 5.1, P = 0.771; 3-month 17.9 +/- 6.7 vs. 17.6 +/- 3.8, P = 0.911). However, VR participants reported significantly higher satisfaction, citing greater engagement, ease of use, and perceived clinical relevance. The VR system was deployed without need for dedicated simulation staff or technical support, demonstrating practical feasibility.CONCLUSIONS:A low-cost VR platform for TEE education is feasible and well received by trainees. Although knowledge outcomes were similar to lecture-based instruction, higher learner satisfaction supports VR as a valuable supplement to traditional methods, particularly in programs with limited access to high-fidelity simulators.

TI Accreditation as a catalyst for improving child nutrition services in
   residential care: A case study
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Accreditation; caregiver training; child nutrition; health policy;
   institutional reform; malnutrition; residential care
AB BACKGROUND:Child nutrition is essential for physical growth, cognitive development, and overall well-being, particularly in residential care institutions that replace family-based care. In Indonesia, accreditation systems were introduced to strengthen the quality of services in Lembaga Kesejahteraan Sosial Anak (LKSA), including nutrition services. However, evidence remains limited on how accreditation influences concrete improvements in child nutrition.MATERIALS AND METHODS:This case study was conducted at LKSA Miftahul Falah, Karawang Regency, West Java Province, Indonesia. Caregiver training enhanced accountability and service delivery. Importantly, child health outcomes improved, with fewer children at risk of malnutrition following the reforms.CONCLUSION:Accreditation served as a catalyst for long-term improvements in child nutrition services at LKSA Miftahul Falah. The experience underscores the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration and evidence-based policy adoption to transform institutional care practices and enhance child welfare outcomes.

TI School-based management: Catalyzing stakeholder engagement for enhanced
   educational quality in Bekasi
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Development; educational quality; engagement; implementation;
   school-based management
ID IMPACT
AB BACKGROUND:Enhancing educational quality through participatory governance is a national priority in Indonesia's primary education sector. School-Based Management (SBM) provides a framework for decentralizing decision-making and strengthening accountability at the school level. Despite its adoption, the impact of SBM on educational equity and quality in rapidly developing regions such as Bekasi City remains underexplored. Understanding how SBM shapes teaching, learning, and stakeholder collaboration is essential for improving educational outcomes.MATERIALS AND METHODS:A qualitative study using realist ethnography was conducted in six purposively selected elementary schools. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with teachers, administrators, and parents, along with classroom observations and document analysis. The Context-Input-Process-Product (CIPP) evaluation model, proposed by Stufflebeam, structured the analysis by examining needs (context), resources (input), implementation strategies (process), and outcomes (product). Thematic coding identified patterns in implementation, resource use, and performance outcomes.RESULTS:Findings showed strong regulatory support and well-prepared human resources. Approximately 90% of evaluated programs met or exceeded national quality standards. SBM implementation improved student performance, attendance, and extracurricular participation, reflecting increased accountability at the school level. However, socio-economic disparities, limited infrastructure, and uneven resource distribution constrained consistent progress across schools.CONCLUSION:SBM fosters holistic educational improvement by promoting collaboration among teachers, parents, and communities. Sustainable institutionalization of SBM requires equitable resource allocation, continuous stakeholder engagement, and context-sensitive implementation. These findings highlight SBM's potential to strengthen educational quality, equity, and community development in Indonesia's primary education sector.

TI A model of moral justice for medical universities: A structural equation
   modeling approach to ethical leadership and organizational integrity
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Ethics; Health Personnel; Health Policy; Job Satisfaction; Justice;
   Leadership; Morals; Organizational culture; Social Responsibility;
   Workplace ethics
AB BACKGROUND:Human resources are central to organizational progress, where moral justice plays a key role in promoting fairness, ethics, and sustainable development. In medical universities-where education, clinical care, and administration intersect-moral justice is crucial for maintaining trust and integrity. However, there is a lack of validated models tailored to this unique context.OBJECTIVE:This study aimed to develop and validate a conceptual model of moral justice tailored to the unique context of medical universities.MATERIALS AND METHODS:A sequential explanatory mixed-methods design was used. In the qualitative phase, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 14 experts (HR directors, department heads, and ethics specialists), selected via purposive and snowball sampling. The interviews lasted 45-60 minutes and were thematically analyzed. Rigor was ensured through triangulation, member checking, and audit trails. Based on qualitative findings, a 36-item questionnaire using a 5-point Likert scale was developed and administered to 256 employees across managerial, technical, and administrative roles at Qom University of Medical Sciences. Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) and Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) were conducted via IBM SPSS Amos, Version 29 (IBM Corp., 2023) to validate the measurement model and assess relationships among the constructs. Model fit was evaluated via Comparative Fit Index (CFI) and Root Mean Square Error of Approximation (RMSEA).RESULTS:The study identified causal factors (e.g., ethical leadership and transparent processes), background factors (e.g., organizational culture and moral values), and intervening factors (e.g., ethical leadership development, and equitable resource distribution) as critical components of moral justice. Strategies such as increasing participation and enhancing accountability were found to drive actionable change, leading to expected outcomes such as transparency, fairness, and increased organizational accountability. The model demonstrated strong fit indices (e.g., CFI = 0.95, RMSEA = 0.05), confirming its validity and reliability.CONCLUSION:The proposed model provides a robust framework for embedding moral justice into organizational structures, emphasizing the interconnectedness of leadership, culture, policies, and strategies. It offers practical recommendations for fostering a culture of trust, fairness, and integrity. Future research should explore the role of technology in enhancing moral justice and expand the model's applicability to diverse organizational contexts.

TI Designing, psychometric, and application of measurement instrument for
   Self-Care Literacy in Prevention of Prostate Cancer (SCL-PCa): A
   mixed-method study protocol
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Instrument; mixed-method; Prostate Cancer (PCa); self-care literacy
AB BACKGROUND:Prostate cancer is one of the most common cancers in men worldwide. Prostate cancer prevention requires self-care; however, there seems to be insufficient information about men's self-care literacy, and almost no studies have addressed this issue. Therefore, this study aimed to design and psychometric evaluation of a measurement instrument for Self-Care Literacy in Prevention of Prostate Cancer (SCL-PCa) in men over 40 years old.MATERIALS AND METHODS:This mixed-method study will adopt a sequential exploratory approach (qualitative-quantitative) and will be conducted in Iran. The initial items for the instrument will be developed in this phase. In the second (quantitative) phase, the instrument's psychometric properties, including face, content, construct validity, and reliability (internal consistency and stability), will be evaluated.CONCLUSIONS:The validated and reliable instrument developed in this study will address the existing gap in assessing prostate cancer-related self-care literacy. Furthermore, it will provide a foundation for designing effective educational interventions and targeted health planning in future research.

TI Effectiveness of unified protocols for transdiagnostic treatment in
   improving the symptoms of depression, stress, anxiety, emotion
   regulation, and cognitive flexibility of students with subclinical
   symptoms of emotional disorders: A randomized clinical trial
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Anxiety; cognitive flexibility; depression; emotion regulation; unified
   protocol
ID COMORBID ANXIETY
AB BACKGROUND:The current study aimed to investigate the effectiveness of unified protocol for the transdiagnostic treatment of emotional disorders (UP) on symptoms of depression, stress, anxiety, emotion regulation (ER), and cognitive flexibility (CF) of students with subclinical symptoms of depression and anxiety disorders.MATERIALS AND METHODS:In this assessor-blinded randomized clinical trial with pretest, post-test, and 6-month follow-up, 30 Farhangian University students in 2024 were selected through convenience sampling and randomly assigned to either an intervention or control group (n = 15 each). TI Antecedents affecting on exit from organizational hostage syndrome
   (Stockholm) in public hospitals
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Organizational hostage syndrome; public hospitals; qualitative content
   analysis; Stockholm syndrome
AB BACKGROUND:The present study aimed antecedents affecting on exit from organizational hostage syndrome (OHS) (Stockholm) in public hospitals.MATERIALS AND METHODS:This study used qualitative content analysis technique. This study fills that gap by identifying a range of antecedents that can influence an employee's ability to exit OHS, including personal, contextual, cognitive, and emotional factors. Moreover, this study offers valuable insights for policymakers and healthcare leaders, who can use the findings to develop more effective strategies for addressing and preventing OHS in public hospitals.

TI Engaging caregivers in providing comprehensive sexual education to
   prevent pregnancy, sexually transmitted infections, and human
   immunodeficiency virus among street adolescents in central Java: A
   quasi-experimental design
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Caregivers; quasi-experimental studies; sex education; street youth
AB BACKGROUND:Prior studies have reported that street adolescents engaging in high-risk behaviors are at a substantially higher risk of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection. This study examines the impact of engaging caregivers on enhancing knowledge, attitudes, and preventive skills against pregnancy, sexually transmitted infections (STIs), and HIV among street adolescents.MATERIALS AND METHODS:A quasi-experimental non-randomized pretest-posttest design with a control group was conducted in Central Java, Indonesia. A total of 200 street adolescents were recruited using purposive sampling, with 100 assigned to the intervention group (Semarang City) and 100 to the control group (Pekalongan and Batang Regencies). The intervention consisted of a six-month comprehensive sexuality education (CSE) program delivered by 20 trained caregivers following a five-day preparatory training. Outcomes included changes in knowledge, attitudes, and sexual risk behavior measured using structured questionnaires. Data were analyzed using Chi-square tests, independent and paired t-tests, and Linear Mixed Models to adjust for baseline differences and repeated measures.RESULTS:This study showed the average score for both knowledge and attitudes was increased by 7.09 and 2.80 points, respectively, after six-month interventions in the intervention group. While sexual risk behavior was decreased from 0.48 to 0.35 (0.7 points). The effectiveness of a six-month comprehensive sexual education intervention by engaging caregivers was revealed by a 56% increase in knowledge and a 21% improvement in attitudes, though positive sexual behavior changes moderately increased by only 16%.CONCLUSIONS:It is recommended that future interventions targeting street adolescents continue to prioritize caregiver engagement as central to these efforts, because their involvement amplifies the intervention's effectiveness and sustainability.

TI The effect of chempuzzle media on the discovery learning
   model toward students' learning outcomes class XI MIPA SMA negeri 4
   maros (study on the subject matter of hydrocarbon compounds)
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE <italic>Chempuzzle</italic>; <italic>discovery learning</italic>;
   education; student
AB BACKGROUND:Students' learning outcomes on hydrocarbon compound material are often suboptimal due to low interest and lack of active participation in the learning process. Innovations, such as the use of educational game media, offer an alternative to improve conceptual understanding. This study is a quasi-experimental research aimed at determining the effect of chempuzzle media within the discovery learning model on the learning outcomes of grade XI MIPA students at SMA Negeri 4 Maros on hydrocarbon compound topics.MATERIALS AND METHODS:This research is a quasi-experiment using a posttest only control group design. The population consists of grade XI MIPA students at SMA Negeri 4 Maros, totaling seven classes. Sampling was conducted randomly, selecting class XI MIPA 5 as the experimental group and XI MIPA 6 as the control group. These classes were chosen because students at this level begin to study more complex chemistry topics, such as hydrocarbon compounds.RESULTS:Descriptive analysis showed that the average learning outcomes of the experimental group were higher than those of the control group. The results confirmed that data from both groups came from homogeneous populations.CONCLUSION:Based on the data analysis, the null hypothesis (H0) is rejected and the alternative hypothesis (H1) is accepted. This indicates a significant effect of using chempuzzle media within the discovery learning model on students' learning outcomes. The media proved more effective than conventional methods as it supports concept building through hands-on experience, critical thinking, collaboration, and contextual learning. Students became more active, motivated, and fully engaged in the learning process.

TI Role of depression, anxiety and stress in predicting body image
   disturbance; the mediating role of shame and guilt in patients with
   breast cancer
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Body image; breast; guilt; psychological distress; shame
ID PSYCHOLOGICAL DISTRESS; WOMEN
AB BACKGROUND:Breast cancer is the most common cancer among women. The treatment process can lead to various physical and psychological challenges. Furthermore, breast cancer treatment can evoke a range of emotions due to changes in body image, including feelings of shame and guilt. This study aims to identify how feelings of shame and guilt mediate the impact of psychological distress on body image difficulties through comprehensive model.MATERIALS AND METHODS:This cross-sectional study, conducted in Tehran, Iran in 2023, recruited 210 breast cancer patients (mean age of 44.50; range 22-75) through convenience sampling. All indirect effects were statistically significant, except for the anxiety and stress scales. This model accounted for 48% of the variance for body image and 29% of shame (R2 = 0.29) and 21% of guilt (R2 = 0.21).CONCLUSION:The findings of this study are expected to advance our theoretical understanding of body image disturbance and provide practical implications for clinical interventions to improve patient's general health and emotional well-being.

TI Developing a hospital response plan for mass casualties in traumatic
   incidents: A study protocol
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Disaster medicine; emergency preparedness; hospital emergency planning;
   mass casualty incidents; trauma centers
AB BACKGROUND:Mass Casualty Incidents (MCIs) are events in which a significant number of individuals sustain injuries, overwhelming the capacity and capabilities of local medical facilities and healthcare centers. Preparedness, along with a well-defined operational and execution plan for managing mass casualties in hospitals, is critical during disasters and emergencies. The absence of such a plan leads to an ineffective response to the incident and a worsening of the conditions in the hospital. This research aims to develop a response plan for managing these incidents in the hospital. MCIs occur when large numbers of people are injured, overwhelming local medical facilities. Having a clear action plan, along with preparedness critical for hospitals to manage these situations during disasters. Without such a plan, responses become ineffective and hospital conditions deteriorate. This research aims to develop a response plan for hospitals to manage these incidents.MATERIALS AND METHODS:This qualitative study will aim to develop a hospital response plan for mass casualties in traumatic incidents in Iran. Initially, a scoping review will be conducted to identify the components and elements of the response plan for mass casualties. Following this, semi-structured interviews will be held to obtain insights from experienced individuals, hospital managers, and experts in the health sector. In the next phase, a focus group discussion will be organized to develop the initial response plan for mass casualties in hospitals in Iran. Finally, the plan will be validated through a simulation and exercise based on a full-scale drill in a hospital. This study involves four phases: a scoping review to identify components, semi-structured interviews with experts, focused group discussions to develop the initial model, and validation through scenario-based drills.CONCLUSION:This study first defines the concept of mass casualties resulting from traumatic incidents and then, by identifying its various dimensions, proposes a hospital response plan for such incidents. This response plan helps hospitals effectively handle such incidents, ensuring optimal and efficient care for casualties.

TI Diet quality in Kazakhstan schools and kindergartens: Implications for
   national nutrition policy
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Child day care centers; diet quality; health policy; Kazakhstan; public
   health; school health services
AB BACKGROUND:Nutrition during preschool and school age plays a crucial role in the development of sustainable dietary habits and is a key determinant of child health. In the context of ongoing revisions to national nutrition standards in Kazakhstan, current evidence on dietary quality in organized educational settings is highly relevant. This study aimed to assess the quality of nutrition among preschool and school-aged children in Kazakhstan and to identify potential gaps in the organization of institutional meal provision.MATERIALS AND METHODS:A cross-sectional study was conducted in 2021-2023 among 700 children and adolescents attending kindergartens and schools in various regions of Kazakhstan. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire covering demographic characteristics, health status, and anthropometric measurements. An integrated Diet Quality Index (0-18 points) was developed, incorporating meal regularity and the frequency of consumption of key food groups. Group comparisons (school vs. kindergarten) were performed using the Chi-square test. Statistical analyses were conducted using IBM SPSS Statistics version 31.0.RESULTS:The median Diet Quality Index score was 12.44 +/- 2.31 (interquartile range 12-13), corresponding to 69.1% of the maximum possible value. Overall, dietary quality was satisfactory; however, structural imbalances were identified. Carbohydrate-rich foods-particularly bread, bakery products, and cereals-contributed most substantially to the overall score. Insufficient consumption of vegetables, fruits, and nutrient-dense foods was observed, despite regular meal patterns.CONCLUSION:Standardized meal provision practices ensure relative uniformity across regions; however, overall diet quality remains suboptimal. The findings highlight the need to improve menu composition and support the continued revision of national nutrition standards. Future studies should include detailed nutrient-level analyses and longitudinal assessments of dietary patterns.

TI Mapping, dynamism, thematic evolution of the scientific production on
   Make up or Beauty products and cancer: A scientometric study
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Beauty products; bibliometrics; cancer; makeup
AB BACKGROUND:In recent years, there has been increasing interest in understanding whether there is a relationship between the use of beauty products and the development of cancer. This study aims to map and analyze the scientific production published on this topic, identifying its evolution, collaboration dynamics, and academic impact.MATERIAL AND METHODS:To comply with transparency and quality, the guidelines defined by the RAMIBS framework when conducting scientometric studies were adhered to. A search was conducted in the Scopus database on March 21, 2025, and 1,996 articles published from 2022 to 2024 were collected. The data were then analyzed by using SciVal and the Bibliometrix package in R Studio. The analytics examined included number of papers, citations per publication, source, author, institution, country, international collaboration, and thematic analysis based on co-occurrence of keywords.RESULTS:Between 2022 and 2025, the analysis revealed an average of 3.7 citations per document, with an average of 7.4 co-authors per article and international participation in 14.8% of the cases. Notable journals included Computers in Biology and Medicine and Medical Physics, and institutions such as the Mayo Clinic and Sun Yat-Sen University. Authors such as Bruns and Wang showed high productivity and impact. The countries with the highest collaboration were the United States, China, and Germany. Thematic analysis identified relevant clusters such as "breast cancer", "deep learning", and "skin cancer", reflecting the evolution of approaches in the area.CONCLUSION:The growing volume of scientific evidence reflects an increasingly collaborative and technologically advanced research landscape. This ongoing expansion underscores the importance of sustained monitoring to better understand the potential cancer-related risks associated with cosmetic product use, ultimately informing safer practices and public health strategies.

TI Developing and validating a functional social relationships enhancement
   program for cancer patients: A Delphi method
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Cancer; Delphi technique; program development; psychosocial
   intervention; social relationship
ID HEALTH; SUPPORT; IMPACT
AB BACKGROUND:Disruptions in key functional aspects of social relationships, such as reduced support, social distress, loneliness, and isolation, contribute significantly to negative patient outcomes. An evidence-based program was designed and evaluated using the Delphi technique to enhance social relationships.MATERIALS AND METHODS:This developmental mixed-methods study, conducted in Isfahan during 2024-2025, designed and validated a program based on the Ewles and Simnett model using a three-round Delphi technique. Healthcare and psychosocial specialists participated, employing structured checklists in all rounds. In the final round, expert consensus exceeded 90% across all evaluated dimensions, confirming the overall credibility and acceptance of the program.CONCLUSION:Experts reached consensus through the Delphi technique to develop and validate evidence-based interventions aimed at improving functional social relationships, providing a practical framework to enhance psychosocial well-being, and strengthening supportive care for cancer patients in clinical and research settings.

TI WIC Online Shopping: Challenges and Opportunities for Vendors and
   Farmers
SO JOURNAL OF NUTRITION EDUCATION AND BEHAVIOR
LA English
DT Article
DE Delphi technique; WIC program; technology; farmers; WIC-authorized
   vendors
ID PARTICIPANTS; DISPARITIES; TECHNOLOGY
AB Objective: This study aimed to expand knowledge and develop a list of technical assistance needs related to the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) online shopping for small, tribal, and rural vendors; farmers; and farmers' markets. Design: A modified Delphi method was used, collecting information via a web-based survey, facilitated workshops, a listening session, and individual interviews from October 2023 to February 2024. Setting: Surveys were distributed through Qualtrics. Zoom was used to conduct virtual workshops, a listening session, and individual interviews. Participants: Purposive sampling techniques were used to recruit the study sample. Of the 435 invited, 239 completed 50% of the survey; 22 survey respondents attended the workshop; 3 tribal vendors and/or farmers attended interview sessions; and 5 non-WIC-authorized vendors, farmers, and farmers' markets attended the listening session. Main Outcome Measure(s): The overall phenomenon of interest included themes related to facilitators and barriers to WIC online shopping. Analysis: Statistical software was used to report descriptive statistics. A rapid qualitative analysis inductive approach was used to construct themes for the study. Results: Facilitators included support and guidance, a robust platform, and feedback mechanisms, whereas barriers included time, resources, and technology. Conclusions and Implications: To ensure WIC online shopping success, it is essential to address both the barriers and facilitators experienced by vendors, farmers, and farmers' markets. While this study collected various perspectives and experiences from merchants, future research may also focus attention on WIC participant perceptions of shopping online with these food retailers.

TI Less Engagement With the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for
   Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) in Early Infancy Predicts Early Exits
   from the Program
SO JOURNAL OF NUTRITION EDUCATION AND BEHAVIOR
LA English
DT Article
DE humans; infant; breastfeeding; pregnancy; WIC
ID RETENTION
AB Objective: Examine how engagement with the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) during the first few months after birth influences continued participation. Design: Secondary analysis of longitudinal data from the WIC Infant Toddler Feeding Practices Study-2. Setting: Eighty WIC sites. Participants: A total of 1,851 study participants completed each postnatal interview through 13 months. Main Outcome Measures: Early exit from WIC (not receiving WIC benefits 6-13 months after birth). Analysis: We predicted early exits as a function of engagement with WIC from enrollment to 5 months after birth using multivariable probit regression models. Results: Study participants were more likely to leave WIC early if they enrolled later in pregnancy (P G 0.05), did not use all WIC food benefits (P G 0.001), did not receive information from WIC on breastfeeding (P G 0.01), did not turn to WIC for information about infant feeding (P G 0.05), or did not use other public assistance programs (P G 0.05). Conclusion and Implications: For participants who initially enroll in WIC, our findings suggest that practices that promote the use of food benefits, reach WIC participants with breastfeeding information, and lead them to look at WIC as a valued source of infant feeding information may promote retention.

TI WIC Participation During Pregnancy and Low and Very Low Birth Weight by
   Race and Ethnicity
SO JOURNAL OF NUTRITION EDUCATION AND BEHAVIOR
LA English
DT Article
DE pregnancy; WIC; low birth weight; very low birth weight; race and
   ethnicity
ID DISPARITIES; OUTCOMES; IMPACT
AB Objective: To examine the association between the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) participation during pregnancy and birth weight by race and ethnicity on a national level. Design: Retrospective cohort of US natality from 2014 to 2022. Setting: All US states and Washington, DC. Participants: First-time mothers of a live singleton birth covered by Medicaid with available data on WIC participation and birth weight. Exposure: WIC participation during pregnancy (yes/no) Main Outcome Measure: Low (<2,500 g) and very low (< 1,500 g) birth weight. Analysis: Multivariable logistic regression Results: A total of 3,778,400 mothers covered by Medicaid were included in this analysis, of which 69.6% were WIC participants during pregnancy. The association between WIC participation and birth weight outcomes differed by race and ethnicity. After adjusting, WIC participants during pregnancy were 25%, 20%, 17%, and 10% less likely to give birth to low-weight infants compared with non-WIC participants for Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islanders, Black, American Indian or Alaskan Native, and White, respectively. Conclusion and Implications: Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children participation during pregnancy was associated with reduced low birth weight in all races and ethnicities. Improving WIC access and participation during pregnancy may support health equity in birth weight outcomes.

TI Investment in Telehealth Is Associated with Cost Savings for Some WIC
   Nutrition Education and Breastfeeding Support Services
SO JOURNAL OF NUTRITION EDUCATION AND BEHAVIOR
LA English
DT Article
DE WIC; telehealth; cost analysis; return on investment; ROI
AB Objective: Estimate startup costs, ongoing service delivery cost savings, and payback period (time to recoup startup costs) of telehealth interventions in the Telehealth Intervention Strategies for Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) project. Design: A return on investment analysis compared pre/post changes in startup costs and ongoing cost savings for interventions that varied by state (1 group-randomized control trial, 4 quasi-experimental matched comparison designs, 1 prepost design). Setting: Local WIC agencies in 6 states (Georgia, Michigan, Wisconsin, North Carolina, South Carolina, and District of Columbia) between February 2022 and September 2023. Participants: Local WIC agencies (n = 31 intervention, n = 25 comparison). Intervention(s): Telehealth interventions varied by state, including enhanced video conferencing and virtual services via customized online platforms. Variables Measured: Startup and ongoing service delivery costs, and payback period. Analysis: Difference-in-difference comparison of costs and return on investment analysis. Results: Startup costs ranged from $147,659 for an existing solution to $1,547,592 for a state agency with many local clinics that received grant-in-aid. Ongoing cost savings in 4/6 (Georgia, Michigan, North Carolina, and District of Columbia) states had a payback period from 1 to 21 months, undiscounted, and < 1 month longer when future savings were discounted. Conclusions and Implications: Savings in ongoing service delivery costs and comparatively short payback period in 4 out of 6 states suggest that telehealth is financially viable for WIC agencies and could provide additional flexibilities and convenience, although a financing source was needed for the original investment in startup costs.

TI Research skills in social education: curriculum, faculty, and
   practitioners
SO PEDAGOGIA SOCIAL REVISTA INTERUNIVERSITARIA
LA English
DT Article
DE Research skills; social education; degree programss; educational
   research
ID RESEARCH-COMPETENCE
AB Research skills plays a key role in fostering evidence-informed practice in Social Education, yet its development across undergraduate programmes remains uneven. This study explores the purpose, role, and scope of research competence by examining both its curricular representation and the perspectives of academic and professional stakeholders. A qualitative design was employed, combining three sources of evidence: an analysis of 38 Social Education curricula from Spanish universities, supported by descriptive statistics to identify curricular patterns; semi-structured interviews with university faculty (n = 8); and two focus groups with Social Education practitioners (n = 12). Results show that research competence is included in all curricula analysed. However, only 36.8 % incorporate an epistemological dimension, 40.0 % address ethical issues, and 60.0 % refer to technological tools. In most programmes, research training is confined to a small number of courses and emphasises methodological skills, limiting its integration into professional practice. Faculty members and practitioners view research competence as essential for critical analysis and the improvement of educational interventions. Both groups highlight the need for stronger links between training and applied research capable of addressing current educational and social challenges. The findings suggest that research training in Social Education should move beyond a narrow academic and instrumental view of research. A broader approach is needed, one that promotes critical inquiry, systematic reflection on practice, and evidence-informed decision-making. Such a shift could strengthen professional identity and improve the quality and relevance of educational interventions in diverse settings

TI Research competencies in social education: a curricular analysis from
   the perspective of ResearchComp in Spain
SO PEDAGOGIA SOCIAL REVISTA INTERUNIVERSITARIA
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Social Education; ResearchComp; research competence; curriculum
   analysis; degree programmes; higher education
AB Research competences are increasingly recognised as a key component of evidence-informed professional practice in the social and educational fields. However, their presence within the initial training of social educators has received limited systematic attention in academic literature. This study analyses the presence and distribution of research competences in the curricula of Social Education degree programmes in Spanish universities, using the European Competence Framework for Researchers (ResearchComp) as the analytical reference framework. A documentary analysis was conducted on the training programmes of 33 Spanish universities and four affiliated institutions, based on the study of 1,406 courses belonging to Social Education degree programmes. The coding process was carried out using a category system grounded in the seven competency dimensions of ResearchComp, complemented by inductive subcodes adapted to the socio-educational field. The results reveal an uneven curricular presence of research competencies. Cognitive competences related to critical thinking and the analysis of socio-educational problems appear more frequently, whereas competences associated with research management, the use of advanced research tools, and the generation of social impact are significantly less visible. In addition, research competences tend to be concentrated on a small number of specific research-related courses, suggesting a fragmented rather than transversal integration within the curriculum. These findings highlight the need to strengthen the transversal integration of research competences in the initial training of social educators and to promote curricular models that embed research more systematically as a core component of professional socio-educational practice.

TI Research skill in higher education in social education: the case of the
   University of Deusto
SO PEDAGOGIA SOCIAL REVISTA INTERUNIVERSITARIA
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Social Education; professional identity; research competence; higher
   education; professional recognition
AB This article aims to analyse the perceptions of students at different stages of their studies and of teaching staff regarding the processes, spaces and moments that facilitate or hinder the development of research skills on the Bachelor's Degree in Social Education at the University of Deusto. The competences of the Bachelor's Degree in Social Education programme and the discourses of 40 individuals (students and teaching staff) were analysed through four focus groups at the University of Deusto. The results analyse research skills in the Bachelor's Degree in Social Education programme not as an additional academic subject, but as a gradual trajectory of linguistic development, contextualised experiences and personal connections. Research skills emerge more as a component of identity in conflict than as a purely operational skill. The study identifies three main discursive shifts: (1) conceptual complexification of research, moving from instrumental definitions to critical and reflective conceptions; (2) broadening of its scope of application, from the academic sphere to socio-educational intervention contexts; and (3) a re-signification of identity, through the transition from an academic requirement to a professional competence constitutive of ethical and rigorous practice. Structural tensions persist, which do not indicate shortcomings in training, but rather a process of professionalisation that is taking root. The development of professional identity depends on the coherent integration of three interrelated dimensions: conceptual, experiential and identity-based. If these spheres converge, research is assimilated as a fundamental aspect of the professional profile; if they become separated, educational fragmentation emerges. The study concludes that professional identity must be understood as the structural core of the professionalisation process in Social Education. Its effective integration requires not only a presence within the curriculum, but also institutional coherence that anticipates its professional legitimisation within the degree programme itself. Rather than an operational challenge, it is a cultural goal aimed at strengthening a professional essence in which practice and research constitute indivisible competencies and guarantees of rigour, validity and social transformation.

TI The research competence in the doctoral programme in sciences of
   education at the University of Granada
SO PEDAGOGIA SOCIAL REVISTA INTERUNIVERSITARIA
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Research skills; doctoral programme; evaluation; quality of education;
   university
AB The present study aimed to analyse the perceived level of development of<br /> the research competencies of the research staff in training on the Doctorate Programme in Educational Sciences at the University of Granada, determining the global and dimensional level, its relationship with sociodemographic and academic variables, and possible areas for improvement. To this end, a quantitative, non-experimental, descriptive and cross-sectional study was carried out. The sample consisted of 71 doctoral students (44 women and 27 men) aged between 23 and 61, enrolled in the programme in the 2024/25 academic year. A questionnaire was used, consisting of sociodemographic and academic data and the Research Comp-based Research Competence Self-Assessment Scale. Data analysis was carried out using descriptive statistics (frequencies, percentages and means), non-parametric tests and multivariate analysis techniques, including principal component analysis and k-means clustering. The results showed a predominance of basic and intermediate global levels, with the presence of advanced and expert levels. Dimensional analysis showed greater development in the cognitive area and lower levels in other dimensions. Additionally, principal component analysis showed an integrated structure of the evaluated competencies, while cluster analysis allowed for the identification of three differentiated competency development profiles (basic, intermediate and advanced-expert). Competence level was related to the year of enrolment, the programme's dedication type and nationality, with no significant association observed with gender or the type of master's programme. Overall, the study provides empirical evidence of the heterogeneity of the development of research skills in the doctoral context and offers relevant information for the design of training, support and improvement strategies for doctoral programmes.

TI Learning to research in social education: systematization of a training
   experience in inclusive contexts
SO PEDAGOGIA SOCIAL REVISTA INTERUNIVERSITARIA
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE research training; socio-educational inclusion; professional skills;
   teaching innovation; Social Education
ID SUSTAINABILITY
AB Research training for university students constitutes an essential pillar in the professionalisation of Social Education, given that professional practice in this field requires grounding interventions in scientific evidence. This article systematises a teaching innovation experience developed at the University of C & oacute;rdoba over four consecutive academic years (2021/2022 to 2024/2025), in which students enrolled in the Bachelor's Degree in Social Education carried out socio-educational research projects in partnership with organisations from the C & oacute;rdoba voluntary and community sector. The experience was structured around the horizontal coordination of subjects, a Service-Learning methodology, and the creation of collective murals linked to the Sustainable Development Goals and to the professional identity of Social Education, involving 499 students and 42 social organisations. A mixed methodology was applied, combining a satisfaction questionnaire, assessment rubrics for the final product, and qualitative analysis using SWOT matrices. The results demonstrate an increasingly positive appraisal by students regarding the professional orientation of the content, the autonomy demanded by the activities, the follow-up provided by teaching staff, and overall satisfaction with the experience. The INCOIN model, by virtue of its longitudinal and integrative nature, stands as one of the principal contributions of this work, as it offers a replicable teaching coordination framework that links research training, Service-Learning and socio-educational inclusion, with potential for transferability to other university contexts. It is concluded that integrating research into the initial training of social educators, through collaborative projects embedded in the social fabric, promotes the acquisition of professional competencies, commitment to inclusion, and the transfer of knowledge to real professional contexts.

TI Conflict mapping: the socio-educational dimension in a homeless shelter
SO PEDAGOGIA SOCIAL REVISTA INTERUNIVERSITARIA
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Homelessness; coexistence; social integration; interpersonal conflicts;
   shelter
AB Homelessness, resulting from structural factors and personal circumstances, negatively affects the exercise of citizenship and the social functioning of those who experience it, leading to both personal and collective deterioration. Shelters, conceived as spaces for coexistence and social integration, are also prone to the emergence of interpersonal conflicts. This study analyzes the conflicts recorded in a shelter for people experiencing homelessness in Santa Cruz de Tenerife, exploring their relationship with variables such as gender, disability, and addiction, as well as associated circumstances, responses, severity, and conflict typology. Using a descriptive exploratory design, 569 incident reports written by staff were analyzed, employing an instrument with 12 categories. Data was processed through descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and cluster analysis using SPSS-26. The most frequent conflicts were relational, linked to disrespect, misuse of services, and rule violations, with a predominance of aggressive verbal responses. Descriptive analysis helped characterize conflict dynamics; chi-square tests revealed significant associations between sociodemographic variables and conflict characteristics; and cluster analysis identified three distinct profiles with differentiated needs and behavioral patterns. These findings highlight the need for personalized strategies combining educational, disciplinary, and mediation measures. The study emphasizes the importance of designing comprehensive interventions that integrate conflict management with socio-educational support, fostering social skills, peaceful coexistence, and the social inclusion of this vulnerable population.

TI Mental health in social educators: occupational factors, needs and
   coping strategies
SO PEDAGOGIA SOCIAL REVISTA INTERUNIVERSITARIA
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Mental health; burnout; Social Education; coping strategies and
   well-being at work
ID PROFESSIONALS; BURNOUT
AB Although educators and social educators work every day with people in very<br /> difficult situations, how they are affected emotionally is rarely discussed. Their work is full of emotional burden, stress and fatigue, and the lack of support, precariousness and difficulty in reconciling work and family life further worsen their mental well-being. In this context, the present study has the general objective of finding out the impact of the work of social educators on their mental health. This objective is specified in three specific objectives: (1) to identify the main work-related factors that influence the mental health of social educators; (2) to find out the mental health needs of social education professionals; and (5) to analyse coping strategies for managing their personal and professional lives. The methodology used is quantitative, and the data collection technique was an anonymous questionnaire created using Google Forms. The sample consisted of 230 practising social educators in different autonomous communities in Spain. The data were analysed using Microsoft Excel tools and JASP software, with descriptive statistics procedures, analysis of association (chi-square tests) and analysis of variance (ANOVA). The results show that most participants experience significant levels of stress and anxiety, feel that their needs are not listened to and consider that work policies are not aligned with their professional reality. In addition, most say that their work affects their personal lives. Although 87.8% use strategies to manage stress, these are mainly individual. Professionals demand improvements in working conditions, training in self-care and greater psychological support. This study makes visible a neglected professional reality and highlights the need for institutions to develop measures to protect the psychosocial well-being of these professionals.

   transforming the perspective of educators
SO PEDAGOGIA SOCIAL REVISTA INTERUNIVERSITARIA
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Educational staff expectations; children and adolescents in care;
   inclusive science education; residential care centers for minors
AB The scientific literature has shown that the expectations of residential care centers staff significantly influence the academic trajectories of children and adolescents under guardianship. However, there is still a lack of knowledge about how direct participation in inclusive science outreach programs can transform educators' perceptions of children and adolescents living in residential care centres, as well as about the impact of these perceptions on their educational pathways.<br /> This article examined the effect of a science education project, funded by the Spanish Foundation for Science and Technology (FECYT), on the expectations of the educational teams of several residential care centers. The project brought current scientific content closer to young people through dialogic encounters and workshops led by active researchers from various disciplines. A qualitative, communicative methodology was employed, including interviews with both the educational staff and the participating adolescents.<br /> The results show that, initially, educators held limited expectations regarding the students' ability to engage with scientific content. However, after observing their active participation, critical thinking, and interest in knowledge, the educational teams reported a shift in their perceptions, acknowledging the academic potential of the participants and valuing their involvement in scientific dialogue.<br /> These findings suggest that inclusive science education programs not only provide meaningful learning opportunities for young people in the child protection system but also help challenge and transform biases among educational staff, fostering more equitable and empowering learning environments.

TI The lens of unconditionality: foster care and the transition to higher
   education among care leavers
SO PEDAGOGIA SOCIAL REVISTA INTERUNIVERSITARIA
LA English
DT Article
DE Higher education; foster care; access to education; equal education;
   school transition
ID SUPPORT; YOUTH; IDENTITY; STUDENTS; PROGRAM; ACCESS
AB Scientific literature shows that young people raised in the child protection system access university or advanced vocational education less frequently. However, a gap remains regarding the role of foster care, as a state protection measure, in shaping these youths' academic trajectories. To address this issue and examine the conditions that enable continued support from foster families after reaching adulthood, a qualitative study using communicative life stories was conducted with four care leavers pursuing higher education and five foster families who supported them in Catalonia. Findings indicate that continued foster family support during higher education enhances emotional well-being and stability, positively influencing academic trajectories. Three enabling factors for sustaining this support were identified: (a) the sustained and unconditional commitment of foster families to young people, (b) youths' self-determination and intrinsic motivation toward education, and (c) institutional, financial, and relational support that legitimizes and sustains these relationships. These results highlight the potential of sustained foster family support as a strategy for social inclusion and underscore the need for policies that recognize this reality to ensure equitable access and success in higher education. Limitations include the absence of data from other educational institutions, pointing to future research on additional actors within the support ecosystem.

TI Day care centers for children and adolescents: impact and challenges of
   socio-educational intervention
SO PEDAGOGIA SOCIAL REVISTA INTERUNIVERSITARIA
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Day care centers for children; adolescence; socialization; risk
   behaviors; community intervention
ID HEALTH-RISK BEHAVIORS; PROGRAM
AB This article examines the trajectories, forms of resistance, and opportunities of adolescents attending day care centers for children and adolescents in the province of Valencia. The study explores the family, community, and personal dimensions that shape their processes of socialization and adaptation to the program. Against the backdrop of current transformations in family and community structures, the research analyzes the factors that facilitate or hinder positive socialization during adolescence. The methodology combines quantitative and qualitative techniques within a mixed-methods approach, enabling the triangulation of objective data and subjective perceptions. This approach aims to inform strategic proposals to strengthen socio-educational intervention from a comprehensive perspective. The main findings reveal greater difficulties in program adaptation among older adolescents, the significant role of family involvement in ensuring continuity within the service, and a strong association between substance use and antisocial behavior. Additionally, limited engagement in community-based and healthy leisure activities was identified, alongside a progressive disengagement from physical territory in favor of more individualized and virtual spaces. Based on these results, the study emphasizes the need to reinforce family involvement and to consolidate community spaces for socialization as key strategies to enhance the effectiveness of socio-educational interventions. Ultimately, it is argued that local institutions should assume an active role in creating mechanisms that foster critical awareness and social learning among adolescents.

TI Family interventions in contexts of vulnerability: barriers and
   opportunities
SO PEDAGOGIA SOCIAL REVISTA INTERUNIVERSITARIA

DT Article

   vulnerable families, networking
ID IMPLEMENTATION; PREVENTION; PROGRAM; PARTICIPATION; DISSEMINATION;
   PARTNERSHIP; STRATEGIES; QUALITY; PARENTS
AB In contexts of social vulnerability, participation in family intervention programs is low. However, there is scientific evidence of the potential of these programs to strengthen vulnerable families and, therefore, the need to implement locally adapted preventive interventions which are integrated into community resources. The community allows for the optimization of preventive family actions, especially in vulnerable social contexts.<br /> In order to evaluate the impact and viability of the Family Competence Program in contexts of family vulnerability, this paper proposes an analysis of the implementation process and the program's impact on participating families. The analysis seeks to identify the factors that have influenced the intervention and that can be addressed for improvement.<br /> The research method is based on a qualitative analysis conducted through focus groups with the professionals responsible for implementing the program in five social service centers. The results of the analysis allow us to identify opportunities and barriers in the intervention process. Families become aware of shared responsibility, strengthen bonds among family members, and establish new connections with other families and professionals. The change in family dynamics is associated with learning communication strategies and conflict resolution. In vulnerable families, the observed changes, although still incipient, strengthen the support provided by social services. Coordination between training professionals and the professionals at social service centers, with whom families have already established relationships, is a key element of participation and is considered essential in their process. The consolidation of family skills programs within the structure of community social services highlights the need to establish networks among family care services, that allows improving-coordination, the generation-of-synergies and optimization of available resources.
