TI Good Food at Home Indianapolis: A Fruit and Vegetable Incentive Model
   Comparing Brick-and-Mortar to Online Ordering
SO JOURNAL OF NUTRITION EDUCATION AND BEHAVIOR
LA English
DT Article
DE food security; grocery stores; food assistance; healthy diet; online
   ordering
ID LOW-INCOME CHILDREN; CO-OP; GROCERY
AB Objective: To compare participant use and satisfaction with nutrition incentives offered through an online platform vs a brick-and-mortar store, following a produce box program. Methods: The intervention group received a produce box program before nutrition incentives (comparison group did not). Within each group, participants were split between a brick-and-mortar store and an online ordering platform for their incentives. Purchasing data and a post survey were collected. Results: Intervention participants used a greater amount of incentives, were more likely to make a purchase, and were more likely to spend all their incentives than the comparison group. Brick-and-mortar participants used a greater amount of their incentives and were more likely to make a purchase, but online ordering participants were more likely to use their full incentive. Conclusions and Implications: Future research is needed to examine and understand spending patterns in nutrition incentive programs, in particular for differences between brick-and-mortar and online ordering opportunities.

TI First-Year Physical Education Teachers' Major Sources of Efficacy:
   Transition From Preservice to In-Service Teaching
SO JOURNAL OF TEACHING IN PHYSICAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE induction; physical education teacher education; continual professional
   development; teaching beliefs
ID CONTENT KNOWLEDGE; EXPERIENCE
AB Purpose: Understanding early career physical education (PE) teachers' experiences and how they influence teaching efficacy is essential for retention amidst reports of teacher attrition and burnout. The purpose of this study was to explore the major sources of efficacy for first-year U.S. PE teachers, which included sources from their preservice to in-service teaching experiences. Methods: As part of a larger study, the study includes individual interviews of first-year PE teachers (N=14) across 11 different U.S. states. Analysis was grounded in Self-Efficacy Theory using both inductive and deductive techniques. Results: Student teaching, observing cooperating teachers, principals, current students, and content knowledge were the reported factors that aligned with their sources of teaching efficacy. Conclusion: The sources of efficacy identified in this study provide insight on how early career teachers develop efficacy, which can be leveraged by both PE teacher education programs and K-12 schools to support retention and growth.

TI Viceroys of the Same Blood: A Comparative Study of Three Cases of
   Fathers and Sons as Viceroys in America
SO REVISTA CIENTIFICA GENERAL JOSE MARIA CORDOVA
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE American history; New Spain; noble careers; Peru; political power;
   viceroys
AB . This article examines three cases in the history of the Habsburg viceroyalty in the Americas where both father and son served as viceroys in New Spain and Peru: the two Marquises of Ca & ntilde;ete; Luis de Velasco, father and son; and the Marquises of Mancera. A comparative study is conducted using three main approaches: the American experience of the viceroys' sons, their courtly careers in Europe, and, finally, their own viceregal tenure in the Americas. The aim is to determine whether any underlying logic can be established to explain this shared trajectory of these nobles, or whether, in reality, the three cases reflect distinct power dynamics and circumstances. The conclusion is that this filial succession was exceptional in the Americas, although the viceroys' family networks were indeed influential. In the case of Luis de Velasco, his experience in the Americas was decisive for his appointment.

TI The Emergence of the Joint Military Concept and the General Command: A
   Review of the War Memoirs (1944-1965)
SO REVISTA CIENTIFICA GENERAL JOSE MARIA CORDOVA
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Armed Forces; defense; General Command; leadership; military strategy;
   organizational change
AB Between 1944 and 1965, the Colombian Armed Forces underwent a profound transformation as a new approach to military affairs emerged. This article analyzes the factors that influenced the establishment of the General Command and the joint military concept by reviewing the War Reports to Congress from those years. It reveals that this transformation was influenced by external factors such as World War II and the Cold War, as well as by internal factors related to public order and the rise of insurgency. TI "The Pen Mightier than the Sword"? The Case for the Collective British
   Political, Diplomatic, and Economic Role in Oman's 1975 Dhofar War
   Success
SO REVISTA CIENTIFICA GENERAL JOSE MARIA CORDOVA
LA English
DT Article
DE Britain; counterinsurgency; Dhofar War; diplomatic influence; economic
   influence; Oman; political influence; UK
ID COUNTERINSURGENCY BRITAIN
AB The defeat of the communist-backed insurgency in Oman's remote Dhofar Province in 1975 can be considered one of Britain's most important counterinsurgency (COIN) successes of the Cold War era. Without sustained British assistance, both Oman and the Gulf would probably have been consigned to communist domination, and Gulf oil supplies to the world held hostage through the Strait of Hormuz. Much of the Dhofar War literature to date has focused either on traditional military aspects of British influence or contribution to the successful campaign, including the role of the 22nd Special Air Service Regiment (SAS) or that of seconded (loaned) officers to Oman. The role, however, of British political, diplomatic, and economic influence and support, and its collective importance in achieving the historic Cold War COIN success in Dhofar has been subsequently largely overlooked. This article outlines this collectively vital contribution towards setting the conditions for achieving a successful COIN outcome. It concludes that the political, diplomatic, and economic influence of Britain on the Dhofar War and its assistance to the Sultanate in this capacity was as, if not more, important than its direct military support in bringing about the defeat of the Dhofari insurgents.

TI Reconsidering Multiple Intelligence Theory: Theoretical and Practical
   Inconsistencies
SO REVISTA DE EDUCACION
LA English
DT Article
DE intelligence; education; multiple intelligences; psychology; methodology
AB The theory of multiple intelligences (MI), proposed by Howard Gardner in 1983, has had a significant impact on the educational field by challenging traditional conceptions of intelligence and promoting pedagogical approaches oriented toward diversity, inclusion, and individualized learning. Since its introduction, MI theory has been widely incorporated into school curricula, teacher education programs, and contemporary educational discourse. However, despite its popularity and practical influence, its status as a scientific theory remains highly contested. This article presents a critical theoretical review of MI that goes beyond the descriptive or pedagogical accounts commonly found in the literature. The analysis systematically examines its main conceptual, logical, and methodological weaknesses, as well as the implications of its uncritical adoption in educational contexts. In particular, the paper addresses the lack of robust empirical evidence supporting the existence of independent intelligences, the ambiguity surrounding the operational definition of "intelligence," and the difficulties involved in developing valid and reliable measurement instruments. These issues are contrasted with alternative models of greater empirical strength, especially the theory of general intelligence (g factor), which is supported by extensive psychometric, neuroscientific, and predictive research. The article's original contribution lies in linking these theoretical critiques to an analysis of the concrete pedagogical uses of MI in educational institutions and teacher training. By doing so, it questions the scientific claims often attributed to such practices and highlights the tension between pedagogical appeal and scientific validity. The paper argues that the continued prominence of MI in education is better explained by its flexibility and intuitive attractiveness than by its empirical rigor. On this basis, the article offers a reflection on the actual scope and limitations of MI in contemporary educational design.

TI Visions of Aragonese teachers on religion as a tool for achieving an
   inclusive education
SO REVISTA DE EDUCACION
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE religious education; teachers; cultural diversity; critical thinking;
   school coexistence; religious literacy; intercultural education
ID SCHOOLS
AB Introduction. The growing cultural and religious diversity in Spanish classrooms demands a rethinking of coexistence and educational equity. This study examines religion teachers' perceptions of the formative value of the subject and its potential to promote religious literacy and critical thinking in plural school contexts. Methodology. A descriptive-correlational mixed-methods design was applied. Participants were 129 religion teachers from different educational stages and school types in the region of Aragon. An ad hoc 19-item questionnaire was used to collect information on the status of the subject, training in religious diversity, classroom practices, and perceptions of coexistence. Descriptive statistics, multiple linear regression with stepwise selection, and thematic categorization of open-ended responses were performed. Quantitative analyses were conducted using SPSS v.25. Results. Teachers assign high importance to the subject (M=3.87/5) but perceive moderate quality (M=2.83) and an unfavorable current situation (M=1.99). They report low student motivation (M=1.71) and a negative impact of educational policies (M=1.04). The inclusion of religious diversity in the classroom is associated with teacher training, educational stage, school type, and teaching experience (R-2=0.252; beta training=0.253). No significant predictors were found for the promotion of critical thinking (F=0.564; p=0.727; R-2=0.022). Regarding coexistence, the most cited problems are misunderstandings, teasing, and discrimination; almost half report no conflicts and view diversity as an opportunity for dialogue. Conclusions. Religious education can foster inclusion if teachers' training in diversity and active, reflective methodologies is strengthened. Institutional support should be reviewed to increase student motivation and curricular coherence. Limitations include the non-experimental design and reliance on self-report data; longitudinal studies and external validation of the instrument are recommended.

TI Development of a self-perception questionnaire to evaluate the design of
   teaching sequences
SO REVISTA DE EDUCACION
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Instructional design; Instructional sequences; Design-Based Research;
   Instrument validation; Formative assessment; Teacher planning;
   Evidence-based practices
ID CONTENT VALIDITY; SAMPLE-SIZE; NUMBER; POWER
AB Design-Based Research (DBR) and Didactical Engineering emphasize the need to evaluate the quality of teaching and learning sequences before their implementation, ensuring internal coherence, solid theoretical grounding, and alignment with students' learning needs. However, the literature reveals a lack of validated instruments that allow for a systematic assessment of initial didactic design quality in non-university educational settings. The aim of this study was to develop and examine the psychometric properties of the Self-Report on Didactic Planning and Sequencing (APSD), an instrument intended for primary and secondary school teachers that assesses design quality across seven dimensions related to evidence-based planning, curricular alignment, differentiation, formative assessment, activity design, inclusion, and iterative improvement. The development process combined an expert-based content validation phase with twelve specialists, followed by an Exploratory Factor Analysis using a sample of 150 teachers. Through principal axis factoring and oblique rotation, the EFA identified six factors that were largely consistent with the theoretical framework. A subsequent Confirmatory Factor Analysis with an independent sample (n = 213) corroborated the expected seven-factor structure and yielded satisfactory model fit indices (CFI= .925; TLI= .919; RMSEA= .041; SRMR= .056). Factor loadings and all dimensions showed adequate internal reliability (ordinal alpha= .72-.91; omega= .68-.89). The findings support the structural validity and practical utility of the APSD as a tool for examining and enhancing the quality of didactic design. The APSD thus offers a grounded, accessible, and theoretically informed resource for educators and researchers seeking to strengthen the quality of teaching sequences before their implementation. The results provide strong evidence of structural validity and reliability, supporting the use of the APSD as a rigorous tool for evaluating and improving the design of instructional sequences.

TI New advances in understanding the initial motivations for pursuing a
   Master's Degree in Secondary Education Teacher Training in Spain: an
   analysis of latent profiles
SO REVISTA DE EDUCACION
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Pre-service teacher education; Student teacher; Motivation; Secondary
   Education; Teacher role; Latent profile analysis
AB In the current dynamic global context, educational systems are confronted with increasing social demands. Consequently, it is essential for secondary education teachers to be rigorously trained, to comprehend the value of education as a trans-formative tool, and to construct a professional identity aligned with the specific characteristics of this educational stage. Previous research has identified diverse motivational profiles among students enrolled on the Master's Degree in Secondary Education Teacher Training in Spain. Within this context, the present study aimed to deepen the understanding of these motivational profiles. The sample comprised 283 students enrolled on the aforementioned Master's programme at a Spanish university. Initially, the measurement scales were validated using Confirmatory Factor Analysis via Structural Equation Modelling. Upon achieving adequate goodness-of-fit indices, a Latent Profile Analysis was conducted. Furthermore, a Chi-square test of independence was employed to identify associations between motivational profile membership and various socio-demographic variables. Seven distinct profiles emerged. Two of these- 'motivated with alternatives' and 'motivated without alternatives'-demonstrated strong alignment with societal expectations regarding the teaching role. The 'low motivation with alternatives' profile exhibited a greater interest in acquiring the qualification than in the teaching profession itself. Conversely, the 'demotivated without alternatives' and 'circumstantial motivation' profiles displayed poor alignment with the expected teaching role. The 'paradoxical' profile revealed a genuine interest in teaching, yet a notably low interest in working with adolescents. Finally, the 'slightly demotivated' profile, exhibiting scores close to the mean, could benefit from targeted interventions to enhance their motivation. Drawing upon these empirical findings, pedagogical measures are proposed to enhance the motivation of pre-service teachers, such as bridging the gap between theory and practice, and incorporating activities that foster self-awareness or facilitate dialogue with in-service teachers.

LA Spanish
DT Article

   education
AB This study presents and empirically applies the Common Good Index in Higher Education (ICGHEI), a composite indicator designed to evaluate higher educa tion institutions (HEIs) from the perspective of common good dynamics, rather than the conventional logic of rankings. Based on the Commons for Higher Education framework, the ICGHEI implements four institutional dimensions- governance, stability, humanity, and justice-through measures based on surveys of students, faculty, and administrative staff. Methodologically, a 76 item com mon good measurement scale was administered to 5,021 participants from nine universities; the DL2 distance metric was used to aggregate the indicators, with the aim of minimizing excessive compensation between dimensions and pro viding multidimensional institutional profiles. Overall, the ICGHEI demonstrates potential as a diagnostic complement to traditional evaluation tools by aligning measu rement with institutional mission and common good commitments. We discuss implications for university management and educational policy, and propose future lines of research, including longitudinal testing, broader national cove rage, and convergent validity studies against external performance indicators.

ID WAGE DIFFERENTIALS; INEQUALITY; GENDER; INVESTMENT; EVOLUTION; SECTOR;
   IMPACT
AB Investment in education is expected to provide significant returns, reflected in higher wages and better employment prospects. However, the returns to education are the result of interactions with the socio-economic context, the productive structure and competition with other human capital. This paper aims to identify the hourly wage differentials of the employees in the Spanish labor market, considering the time evolution and the educational expansion. TI How mathematical games shape pre-service teachers' generalization
   processes: a qualitative case study
SO REVISTA DE EDUCACION
LA English
DT Article
DE Mathematics education; Mathematical games; Mathematical generali sation;
   Pre-service teachers; Case study
ID SCIENCE
AB This study investigates how pre-service mathematics teachers engage in mathematical generalization within game-based learning environments. Although game-based learning has gained increasing attention in mathematics education, existing research has largely emphasized engagement, motivation, and achievement, with comparatively limited focus on how such environments support the development of mathematical generalization processes. In particular, little is known about how pre-service teachers transition from concrete gameplay experiences to symbolic reasoning and formal mathematical generalizations, or how these processes relate to justification and proof. Addressing this gap, the study employed a qualitative multiple case study design involving 28 pre-service mathematics teachers enrolled in a Teaching Mathematics with Games course at a public university. Grounded in constructivist and problem-solving perspectives, the study examined how participants' actions, representations, and discussions during gameplay contributed to emerging generalizations. Data were collected through classroom observations, audio-recorded whole-class and small-group discussions, participants' written artifacts produced during gameplay, and researcher field notes. Participants played mathematical games, documented observations, identified patterns, and attempted to formulate and justify generalizations. The data were analyzed using qualitative analysis techniques supported by illustrative excerpts from participants' discourse and written work. Findings indicate that most participants actively generated predictions, drew inferences, and relied on intuitive reasoning during gameplay. However, many experienced difficulties in constructing valid and general mathematical statements and in justifying their conclusions through formal reasoning. These results reveal persistent challenges in the interconnected practices of generalization and proof, despite the exploratory and engaging nature of game-based environments. The study highlights the need for structured pedagogical support to help pre-service teachers transform exploratory insights into mathematically justified generalizations.

TI Decoding the paradox: How high school students sustain English as a
   foreign language learning engagement despite boredom
SO REVISTA DE EDUCACION
LA English
DT Article
DE boredom; engagement; EFL learning; LPA; intraindividual differences
ID ACHIEVEMENT; CHINESE; EMOTIONS
AB Boredom is often viewed as a negative predictor of engagement in English as a foreign language (EFL) learning, yet research on how boredom and engagement vary among learners is limited, particularly in exam-driven Chinese high school EFL contexts. This study examines intraindividual differences among Chinese high school EFL students using an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design. In Study 1, Latent Profile Analysis (LPA) using Mplus 8.7 identified four groups from a sample of 416 students: low boredom-high engagement (24.3%), high boredom-low engagement (29.6%), moderate boredom-moderate engagement (38.0%), and high boredom-high engagement (8.2%). The unexpected "high boredom-high engagement" group challenges the assumption that boredom always leads to disengagement. Hence, in Study 2, qualitative interviews with 33 students were conducted to explore the underlying antecedents and coping strategies of this group. Thematic analysis using MAXQDA 2022 revealed that engagement was driven by extrinsic motivation, relational duty, aspiration-based motivation, and internal drive. Students employed dual-track coping strategies, including in-class techniques (e.g., self-guidance, cognitive reframing, and gamified learning) and everyday strategies (e.g., mindset adjustment, habit formation, and cultural connection), reflecting both real-time classroom regulation and longer-term resource building. These findings highlight the psychological factors that enable students to stay goal-oriented in challenging situations. For EFL teaching, it may be more productive to build motivational support systems and teach coping strategies than to attempt to eliminate boredom altogether.

TI Teacher Quality Evaluation: International and Regional Perspectives
SO REVISTA ESPANOLA DE EDUCACION COMPARADA
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Teacher evaluation; teacher quality; teacher professional development;
   comparative education; accountability; education policy
ID DEVELOPING-COUNTRIES; EDUCATION
AB Teacher performance evaluation constitutes one of the most contested axes of contemporary education policy, as it brings together demands for accountability with objectives related to professional development and the regulation of the teaching profession. From a comparative education perspective, this article examines how different education systems have addressed these tensions through their teacher evaluation policies, with the aim of identifying the meanings attributed to evaluation, the purposes that guide their design, and their implications for professional practice and teaching careers. The study adopts a descriptive-analytical comparative approach, based on a documentary and regulatory review of teacher performance evaluation systems in countries regarded as international benchmarks in the specialized literature, Australia, Ontario (Canada), the United Kingdom, New Zealand, Singapore, the Republic of Korea, Estonia, and the United States, as well as three Latin American cases with consolidated institutional trajectories, Chile, Colombia, and Peru. In addition, emerging challenges are identified concerning the recognition of continuous professional learning, the consideration of different phases of the teaching career, the valuation of peer collaboration, and the ethical and pedagogical integration of artificial intelligence. The article provides relevant comparative insights to inform the design of contextualized teacher evaluation policies oriented towards educational improvement.

   Inspection and Peer Observation in China
SO REVISTA ESPANOLA DE EDUCACION COMPARADA
LA English
DT Article
DE teaching quality evaluation; dual-track governance; administrative
   inspection; peer observation; institutional pillars; policy
   recontextualisation
ID POLICY
AB Teaching quality evaluation is a central instrument of contemporary education governance, yet many educa-tion systems privilege either accountability-oriented inspection or development-oriented professional learning within a single evaluative framework. This study examines China as a distinctive case in which administrative inspection and peer observation are formally institutionalised as parallel, policy-mandated mechanisms. Rather than treating these mechanisms as isolated practices, the study conceptualises teaching quality eval-uation as a dual-track policy system shaped by multiple institutional pillars and enacted across governance levels. Drawing on institutional theory, policy enactment theory, and cultural-historical perspectives, the study conducts a comparative qualitative analysis of 98 policy documents issued between 2010-2025 at national, provincial, and school levels. The corpus covers seven provinces/municipalities selected to capture variation in economic development and administrative capacity. The findings reveal that policy documents construct administrative inspection as operating through a vertically extended, consequence-bearing accountability chain grounded in the regulative institutional pillar. In contrast, peer observation is discursively positioned within horizontally organised professional structures rooted in the normative pillar of collegial learning. The two tracks are deliberately differentiated yet connected through selective and asymmetrical coupling mecha-nisms, including artefact circulation and improvement-oriented sequencing. Cross-provincial analysis reveals strong structural convergence alongside systematic variation in policy elaboration: functional differentiation is achieved primarily in well-resourced contexts, while less-resourced provinces display thinner professional learning infrastructure. The study contributes to international debates on teaching quality evaluation by pro-posing "dual-track governance" as an alternative to systems that either privilege one orientation or attempt integration within single instruments. Rather than a definitive solution, this concept frames China's config-uration as a large-scale policy experiment. This arrangement addresses the formative-summative tension by institutionalising accountability and development as parallel, coordinated tracks with distinct purposes and explicit boundary mechanisms. As the analysis draws on policy documents, it illuminates governance architecture rather than teachers and teaching effects. It raises comparative questions for systems where inspection and professional development lack formal coordination.

TI The teacher evaluation programs in mexican basic education: the
   improvement of accountability
SO REVISTA ESPANOLA DE EDUCACION COMPARADA
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE teacher evaluation; teachers; basic education; normative evaluation;
   professional career
AB Mexico has a significant track record in evaluation programs for primary school teachers that aim to improve quality. In relation to this, we analyze three programs-Carrera Magisterial (1993-2015), Servicio Profesional Docente (2013-2018), and Sistema de Carrera (2019-present)-in order to understand their continuities, approaches, and changes regarding teacher evaluation. In this regard, we conducted a document-based study, consisting of a corpus that included presidential decrees, laws, regulations, official agreements, profiles, indicators, and guidelines related to the selected evaluation programs. The results suggest that since the 1990s, the country established a teacher evaluation system for accountability purposes, initially solely to allocate salary incentives, and later to regulate admissions, promotions, and tenure within the teaching profession. The programs show refinement in their instruments and requirements to improve the efficiency of teacher management. However, little attention has been given to designing an evaluation system that monitors the challenges teachers face in classroom work, their school context, and teaching practices.

DE Higher Education; Institutional Evaluation; Educational Improvement;
   Accountability; Teacher Supervision
AB This study analyzes the evaluation of teaching quality in higher education through existing university inspection models in Spain, from a comparative education perspective, with the aim of analytically grounding an integrated model that balances regulatory supervision with pedagogical support and continuous improvement. The research combines a documentary and functional comparative analysis of inspection service regulations with an assessment of the viability of university inspection at the University of the Balearic Islands (EVIU-UIB), based on a survey administered to its university community. TI Evaluation for improvement or control? Professional development and
   institutional tensions in Ibero-American Higher Education: the cases of
   Spain and Ecuador
SO REVISTA ESPANOLA DE EDUCACION COMPARADA
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Teacher evaluation; Evaluation methods; Public policies; Educational
   Quality; Career development; Teacher competencies
ID SYSTEMS; QUALITY; IMPACT
AB This article presents a comparative analysis of university teaching quality evaluation systems in Spain and Ecuador, with the aim of identifying their similarities, differences, tensions, and challenges. The study examines current regulations, the institutional structures responsible for evaluation, the instruments applied, and the predominant approaches in both countries. Despite structural differences, both contexts reveal a discourse oriented toward continuous improvement and 360 degrees evaluation, yet with persistent tensions between institutional control and professional development, as well as limited feedback mechanisms to effectively foster teaching enhancement. Among the most representative findings, it is highlighted that in Spain, teaching evaluation is voluntary, which limits its scope, and is strongly linked to accreditation and promotion processes. At the national level, it is coordinated through ANECA, which implements the PEP, ACADEMIA, and DOCENTIA programs; however, the evaluation process is highly decentralized in regional quality agencies, occasionally resulting in territorial inequalities. Furthermore, there is an overemphasis on scientific publications as the main evaluative criterion, to the detriment of other aspects such as educational innovation or community engagement. In contrast, in Ecuador, evaluation is mandatory, centralized, and linked to the continuity of employment for teaching staff under the regulations and procedures set by the Council of Higher Education (CES). A predominantly instrumental and punitive perception of evaluation prevails among faculty members, often leading to adaptive practices aimed at meeting predefined indicators rather than embracing evaluation as a formative tool. In conclusion, the study reveals tensions between professional development and institutional control, as well as between university autonomy and higher education regulatory frameworks in both countries.

TI Between Appreciation and Resistance: Teachers' Meanings Regarding
   Chile's Inclusion Law
SO REVISTA ESPANOLA DE EDUCACION COMPARADA
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Inclusion Law; Teachers; Meanings; Tensions; Challenges.
ID EDUCATION
AB The education system in Chile is currently experiencing a period of tension and change as a result of a series of reforms aimed at altering the privatized and market-oriented orientation that has long characterized the sector. Within this context, the implementation of the Inclusion Law constitutes a key reform, as it abolishes student selection mechanisms with the objective of reducing educational segregation. Accordingly, this article seeks to examine the meanings attributed to the Inclusion Law by teachers working in medium-and high-performing schools. The study adopts a qualitative research design, using semi-structured interviews as the primary data collection method. The participants were 19 teachers from privately managed, publicly funded schools in the Valparaiso Region. Data were analyzed using content analysis. The findings reveal the tensions experienced by teachers as a result of the implementation of the Inclusion Law. While the reform is recognized as a necessary process, it is simultaneously resisted due to the elimination of student selection procedures, which leads to increased student diversity for which schools are perceived as insufficiently prepared. Overall, the results indicate that the implementation of the Inclusion Law in medium-and high-performing schools has been met with significant resistance, as it disrupts classroom homogeneity and complicates pedagogical and instructional practices.

TI Educational Policies and Measures for Intellectual Diversity: A
   Comparative Study of Spain and Italy
SO REVISTA ESPANOLA DE EDUCACION COMPARADA
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Inclusive education; intellectual diversity; attention to diversity;
   educational legislation; comparative education policies
AB Inclusive education, a key objective of global and European educational policy, is comparatively analyzed in this article, which examines policies and measures for addressing intellectual diversity in Spain and Italy. Using a qualitative approach, key dimensions are addressed, such as the legal framework, student categorization, the philosophical model, schooling modalities, resources, curricular measures, evaluation processes, family participation, and institutional autonomy. This situation is aggravated by insufficient resources and funding, which limit the elimination of barriers and reasonable adjustments. This contrast enriches the understanding of inclusion as a social and ethical project that demands sustained commitment, systemic coordination, and educational justice.

TI Regulating artificial intelligence in Higher Education: an exploratory

DT Article
DE Artificial Intelligence; USA; Higher Education; Universities;
   Regulation; Ethics
ID TRANSLATION
AB Higher education institutions need to carefully consider how effective and appropriate their approaches are to learning, teaching and assessing the use of artificial intelligence (AI) as a way to improve the quality of their role in a constantly evolving society. There has been a significant increase in the perceived opportunities and challenges around AI, and some higher education institutions have begun to develop policies on the impact of AI on university life. However, to date no studies have critically analyzed how higher education institutions are regulating AI. Therefore, the aim of this study is to analyze the regulations established by universities in two countries (United States and Spain) on the use of AI in higher institutions. The aim is not penalizing or limiting but adding to AI fundamental criteria and guidelines for use. In addition, this paper finds that there is no solid policy on how to approach the epistemological challenge raised by AI in research. The current study and future ones on AI are part of an emerging and significant development in educational research that alludes to the study of the AI narrative.

TI Comparative study about Initial Teacher Training of Primary Education in
   the context of Mercosur
SO REVISTA ESPANOLA DE EDUCACION COMPARADA
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Initial teacher training; quality of education; comparative education;
   Mercosur
ID POLICIES
AB Initial Teacher Training (ITT) is fundamental to the preparation of future educators, as it lays the foundation for quality education in educational systems. In the context of Mercosur, this training phase encompasses a variety of structures and approaches across member countries. Therefore, this research aims to establish the convergences, divergences, and trends in ITT models for Primary Education. To this end, a comparative study was conducted using qualitative research through the analysis of official documents from countries such as Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay, which share historical and cultural similarities. The results and conclusions reveal that these similarities and differences provide a comprehensive overview of ITT in the region, allowing for reflection on the challenges faced in this process to contribute to modernization and the improvement of school effectiveness. The trends identified indicate an increasing concern regarding the quality and uniformity of ITT, which could favor teacher mobility and collaboration between countries. Despite the differences found, it is observed that these countries share the challenge of promoting cooperation and complementarity within the framework of regional integration, taking into account the opportunities and challenges arising from the level of economic and social development of each country compared.

TI Examining National Science Assessments: A Comparison of NAEP and NAFES
SO REVISTA ESPANOLA DE EDUCACION COMPARADA
LA English
DT Article
DE National assessments; NAFES; NAEP; comparative study; science education
AB This study seeks to conduct a comparison between national assessments in science, specifically the NAEP national assessment implemented in the United States and the NAFES national assess-ment implemented in Saudi Arabia. The research employs a qualitative comparative analysis of the NAEP and NAFES assessments. Key components analyzed include the assessment frame-works, types of questions used, administrative processes, and the resultant impact on educational policies. The results of the study concluded that both assessments are important tools for evaluating education; however, there are some differences. NAEP focuses on scientific practices in assessment, while NAFES emphasizes cognitive levels. The questions in the NAEP assessment are diverse, including practical and interactive tasks, whereas NAFES primarily relies on multiple-choice questions. In terms of administrative procedures, both assessments aim to implement systematic steps, but they differ in the duration of the administered tests and the samples used. NAEP focuses on the depth of assessment through random sampling, whereas NAFES empha-sizes administering a test to all students. Regarding the impact of the assessments on educational policies and practices, we find that the NAFES assessment places significant emphasis on accountability and competition among schools, while the NAEP assessment has a broader impact on curriculum development and educational reforms. The study recommends that NAFES could significantly benefit from adopting practices established by NAEP, such as incorporating a wider variety of question types and emphasizing scientific practices to better prepare students for real-world challenges. It also highlights the importance of using assessment results to improve educational practices and provide valuable insights for specialists, policymakers, and educators.

TI Rurality and School Leadership: The Displacement of Pedagogical
   Leadership in Schools in Alhue
SO REVISTA GESTION DE LA EDUCACION
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE SCHOOL LEADERSHIP; EDUCATION POLICY; SCHOOL VULNERABILITY; RURALITY
AB This article examines how rurality and school vulnerability shape the exercise of school leadership and generate tensions in the relationship between principals and teachers in municipal schools in the commune of Alhue (Chile). The objective of the study is to analyze the gap between the pedagogical leadership promoted by national education policy and the leadership effectively exercised in rural contexts, as well as its effects on school climate and teacher participation. A qualitative case study with an exploratory and interpretative approach was conducted. The research included semi-structured interviews with 25 participants (10 school leaders and 15 teachers) from the five municipal schools in the commune, together with a documentary analysis of national regulations and institutional documents. The analysis was carried out through thematic coding and triangulation of sources, considering data collected between 2019 and 2023. The results reveal a mismatch between normative leadership expectations and the organizational conditions of the territory. The administrative and teaching overload of school leadership teams, role ambiguity, limited pedagogical presence in classrooms, and teacher participation perceived mainly as formal create scenario in which leadership is primarily oriented toward institutional functioning and administrative compliance. The study proposes understanding this phenomenon as a structural displacement of instructional leadership, in which instructional functions do not disappear but become subordinated to organizational demands. This finding helps explain the gap between educational policy and school practice and highlights the need for policies that recognize the structural conditions of rural territories.

TI Effectiveness of AST-120 and probiotics (lactobacillus) on renal
   function in patients with chronic kidney disease: A retrospective cohort
   study from the TriNetX global collaborative network
SO SCIENCE PROGRESS
LA English
DT Article
DE chronic kidney disease; AST-120; protein-bound uremic toxins; real-world
   evidence; propensity score matching
ID INDOXYL SULFATE; CARDIOVASCULAR OUTCOMES; ADSORBENT AST-120; EPPIC
   TRIALS; GUT; PROGRESSION; MECLOFENAMATE; MICROBIOTA; EVENTS
AB Objective Chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression has been associated with the accumulation of protein-bound uremic toxins (PBUTs), such as indoxyl sulfate and p-cresyl sulfate. AST-120, an oral carbon adsorbent, and probiotics (e.g., Lactobacillus) have been used in clinical practice to modulate PBUT burden, but comparative real-world data on long-term outcomes remain limited. Methods We conducted a retrospective, multinational study using de-identified electronic health records from TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Adult patients (>= 18 years) with baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate <60 mL/min/1.73 m(2) who received AST-120 or Lactobacillus between January 2001 and July 2025 were identified. After 1:1 propensity score matching on 16 baseline covariates, 340 patients were included in each group. Primary outcomes were progression to stage 4 or 5 CKD, end-stage kidney disease (ESKD), and all-cause mortality. Time-to-event analyses were performed using Cox proportional hazards models. Results Over mean follow-up of 2.3 years, AST-120 use was associated with lower risks of progression to stage 4 CKD (HR 0.294; 95% CI 0.148-0.586), stage 5 CKD (HR 0.488; 95% CI 0.296-0.805), ESKD (HR 0.333; 95% CI 0.168-0.663), and all-cause mortality (HR 0.508; 95% CI 0.351-0.735), compared with a probiotic-exposed reference cohort. The composite outcome of ESKD or mortality showed a similar association. Conclusions In this propensity score-matched real-world cohort, AST-120 use was associated with more favorable renal and survival outcomes compared with a probiotic-exposed reference population. Given the observational design and potential for residual confounding, these findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating.

TI Intelligent coal mining: An approach to generating optimal Shearer's
   cutting trajectories
SO SCIENCE PROGRESS
LA English
DT Article
DE navigation mining; the shearer; trajectory optimization; the genetic
   algorithm
AB Intelligent unmanned mining technology is very important for modern coal mining to improve the safety and efficiency. Autonomous navigation cutting technology is an emerging trend of intelligent fully mechanized coal mining technology. This paper presents the construction method of the accurate 3D coal seam model as determination of the navigation map of the shearer. The cutting plane implicit function was induced to generating the section of the coal seam model, and the coal seam roof and floor boundary curves were achieved by the cubic B-spline curve fitting. By comparing the optimization effects of the BP neural network, the RBF neural network and the genetic algorithm, the genetic algorithm is finally selected for the shearer drum cutting trajectory optimization to reduce the gangue rate and improve the coal recovery rate. The simulation steps of the genetic algorithm are described in the paper, whose experimental results show that after 100 generations of optimization by the genetic algorithm. The maximum error of the cutting trajectory is reduced to 0.017 m, which is significantly better than the cubic B-spline fitting results before optimization. The findings of the paper provide the theoretical and technical support for the development of intelligent navigation mining technology of the shearer.

AB Objective To evaluate the accuracy of ultrasound-based fetal weight estimation and to develop and internally validate a prediction model for low birth weight.Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted among 269 individuals.Results The accuracy of ultrasound weight estimation was 72.9%, with 27.1% of estimates falling outside +/- 10% of actual birth weight. The Pearson correlation for estimated fetal weight and actual birth weight was 0.92. Using LASSO regression eight predictors were selected and entered in the multivariable analysis of which gestational age, estimated fetal weight, timing of estimation, and placental location were found significant. The original model demonstrated strong discrimination of AUC of 95.9% 95%CI (93.1-98.0%), and good calibration. Internal validation via 1000-bootstrap resampling yielded a bias-corrected AUC of 94.3%, indicating preserved predictive performance with minimal optimism. An integer-based risk score was derived to enhance clinical usability. The risk score model achieved acceptable discrimination (AUC = 76.8%, 95% CI: 70.0-83.0%) and good calibration (p = 0.301). Agreement between the full prediction model and the simplified risk score was fair (Cohen's Kappa = 0.353, p < 0.0001), indicating that the simplified score is best suited as a pragmatic bedside risk-stratification tool rather than a direct substitute for the full model. Women were stratified into low (0-10 points), medium (11-21), and high-risk (22-36) groups corresponding to increasing predicted probabilities of low birth weight (3.2%-96.3%).Conclusion Ultrasound-based fetal weight estimation using the Hadlock-III formula indicated acceptable accuracy and strong correlation with actual birth weight. We developed and internally validated prediction model for low birth weight with excellent discrimination, good calibration, and predictive value beyond estimated fetal weight alone. A risk-score tool was created to facilitate rapid bedside risk stratification. However, given the single-center nature of the study and the absence of external validation, further multicenter validation is required before broader clinical implementation.

TI Initial stress effects on fractional thermoelastic wave propagation in
   semiconductor media under three thermoelasticity theories
SO SCIENCE PROGRESS
LA English
DT Article
DE initial stress; fractional derivatives; semiconductor; refined
   dual-phase-lag model
ID VOIDS
AB This work examines the impact of initial stress on the spread of coupled thermo-mechanical waves in a semiconductor thermo-elastic medium using a beta-order fractional derivative model. The study is undertaken utilizing three generalized thermo-elastic theories: Dual-Phase-Lag (DPL) model, Lord-Shulman (L-S) theory, and Refined Dual-Phase-Lag (RDPL) model. To accurately reflect the underlying physical processes, the governing equations for heat conduction, elastic deformation, and semiconductor carrier dynamics are fully coupled, taking into account both finite-speed thermal transport and carrier density effects. To simplify the mathematical treatment, a suitable nondimensionalization strategy is adopted, lowering the number of governing parameters and clarifying the structure of the problem. A transform technique is then utilized to transform the resulting system of coupled partial differential equations (PDEs) into an analogous system of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) that can be solved analytically. This approach produces solution for displacement, temperature, carrier density, and stress tensor components, allowing for a complete investigation of wave propagation properties inside the medium. Numerical simulations using graphical representations are used to investigate the physical significance of the theoretical concept. These computations provide a comparative examination of physical quantities with and without initial stress across the three thermo-elastic theories. The beta-fractional derivative and initial stress significantly impact wave behavior, including propagation velocity, amplitude evolution, and attenuation characteristics. Furthermore, the analysis sheds further light on the interplay between thermal processes and carrier density effects in thermo-elastic materials, emphasizing the significance of these elements in precisely forecasting the dynamic response of modern semiconductor media.

TI Exploration of the potential utilization value in Cordyceps
   militaris substrate after industrial cultivation in terms of
   nutritional and pharmaceutical applications
SO SCIENCE PROGRESS
LA English
DT Article
DE <italic>Cordyceps militaris</italic>; substrate; bioactive ingredients;
   volatile components; utilization value; optimum drying parameters
ID SUBMERGED CULTURED MYCELIA; CHEMICAL-COMPOSITION; FRUITING BODIES;
   MEDICINAL VALUE; POLYSACCHARIDES; COMPONENTS; PATHWAY
AB Objective A large number of substrates after harvesting the fruiting bodies of Cordyceps militaris have been discarded or only used as feed and fertilizer. In this study, we aimed to investigate the potential utilization value of residual substrates under industrial cultivation of C. militaris.Methods The various bioactive substances in C. militaris fruiting body and substrate were measured and compared by colorimetry, HPLC, burning method, Kjeldahl legal nitrogen method, and GC-MS et al. TI LncRNA AK093407-IFITM1-Wnt/β-catenin regulation axis in colorectal
   cancer
SO SCIENCE PROGRESS
LA English
DT Article
DE colorectal cancer; LncRNA; IFITM1; Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway
ID CELL-PROLIFERATION; SIGNALING PATHWAY; CATENIN PATHWAY; APOPTOSIS;
   INVASION; ANTIBODY; SURFACE; TARGET
AB Objective Colorectal cancer (CRC) carries high morbidity and mortality worldwide. IFITM1 serves as a potential independent prognostic factor for CRC metastasis and advanced stages, partly through regulating the Wnt/beta-catenin pathway. LncRNA AK093407 is upregulated in CRC and promotes cancer cell proliferation, but its regulatory mechanism remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the biological function of LncRNA AK093407 in CRC progression and clarify its regulatory mechanism on IFITM1 and the Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway.Methods This in vitro study included clinical tissue samples from 22 CRC patients and human CRC cell lines. Proteomic analysis was applied to screen potential downstream targets of AK093407. The expression levels of AK093407 and IFITM1 in clinical tissues and cell lines were detected by qRT-PCR. Lentiviral infection and siRNA transfection were used to establish overexpression and knockdown models. MTT, colony formation, transwell, wound healing, and flow cytometry assays were performed to assess cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and apoptosis. Western blotting was used to measure key proteins in the Wnt/beta-catenin pathway. Subcellular fractionation and RIP assays were used to explore the molecular mechanism.Results LncRNA AK093407 and IFITM1 were both significantly highly expressed in CRC tissues and cells. Overexpression of AK093407 or IFITM1 markedly enhanced proliferation, migration, and invasion and inhibited apoptosis. Knockdown of IFITM1 reversed the oncogenic effects induced by AK093407 overexpression, while IFITM1 overexpression rescued the phenotypic changes caused by AK093407 silencing. Mechanistically, IFITM1 activated the Wnt/beta-catenin pathway and directly interacted with beta-catenin.Conclusions LncRNA AK093407 promotes CRC malignant progression by upregulating IFITM1 and activating the Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway, forming a novel AK093407-IFITM1-Wnt/beta-catenin regulatory axis. These findings identify a potential diagnostic and therapeutic target for CRC, although further in vivo validation is warranted.

TI Situated AI ethics: a cultural-historical and ecological framework for
   education
SO COMPUTERS AND EDUCATION OPEN
LA English
DT Article
DE AI ethics; Cultural-historical activity theory; Ecological systems
   theory; Situated learning; Transformative agency
AB This paper proposes a situated approach to AI ethics in education, grounded in Cultural-Historical Activity Theory (CHAT) and ecological systems theory, to conceptualize how ethical decision-making around AI emerges across interconnected individual, institutional, cultural, and geopolitical contexts. Moving beyond universalist and principle-based ethics frameworks, we frame AI as a non-neutral socio-technical assemblage whose ethical implications are historically produced and locally negotiated. The framework is applied to a comparative analysis of 7 national cases (Australia, Finland, England, France, Italy, New Zealand, and South Korea), mapped across five ecological levels: self, classroom/group, state/geopolitical, cultural norms, and global. The analysis reveals recurring tensions between innovation agendas and ethical concerns, including uneven teacher autonomy, regulatory overload, fragmented policy guidance, cultural anxieties about automation, and global pressures related to competitiveness, labour markets, and platform dependence. Across contexts, teachers are frequently positioned as moral gatekeepers of AI use while lacking adequate structural, institutional, and epistemic support to exercise ethical agency. By integrating CHAT's attention to contradictions, power relations, and transformative agency with an ecological perspective on nested systems, the paper demonstrates that ethical AI practices are not implemented through compliance but negotiated through situated action. We argue that ethical engagement with AI requires context-sensitive, collective, and transformative approaches that extend AI literacy beyond technical skills toward critical, political, and ecological forms of agency.

TI Operationalizing cognitive apprenticeship through generative AI
   pedagogical agents: Proactive and contextualized guidance in
   simulation-based learning
SO COMPUTERS & EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Computer simulations; Generative AI; Cognitive apprenticeship;
   Pedagogical agent; In-context guidance
ID COMPUTER-SIMULATIONS; FRAMEWORK
AB Computer simulations can support science learning by making scientific phenomena visible and manipulable, but students often struggle to connect simulation observations with underlying mechanisms. This study draws on Cognitive Apprenticeship (CA) theory to design and examine a CA-based generative AI (GenAI) pedagogical agent (CA agent) that provides proactive and contextualized scaffolding during simulation-based learning. Using a contrastive comparison, the study compared the CA agent with a reactive Q&A agent. Data from 53 high school students included pre- and post-tests, student-agent dialogues, students' simulation actions, and the agent's internal reasoning records. Quantitative analyses, dialogue coding, Epistemic Network Analysis (ENA), and qualitative case analyses were used to examine learning processes and outcomes. The ENA and case analyses revealed four patterns of students' epistemic engagement with the CA agent: epistemic outsourcing, the observation-modeling gap, AI-mediated model initiation, and progressive scientific modeling. In addition, the agent's evaluation levels were associated with students' learning outcomes, while case studies of the evaluation records showed that the CA agent's reasoning process was adaptive to the dialogue context but remained primarily conceptoriented, sometimes overlooking students' observational difficulties and their need to exercise epistemic agency. Compared with the reactive Q&A agent, the CA agent showed a marginal advantage in supporting application-oriented learning, and students' application gains varied across different epistemic engagement patterns. This study contributes to research on GenAIsupported simulation-based learning by clarifying how CA-agent scaffolding was associated with students' epistemic engagement and by revealing the affordances and limitations of the CA agent.

TI Modelling leadership capacity for digital curriculum transformation and
   students' engagement: A mediated model based on the advanced higher
   education framework
SO CONTEMPORARY EDUCATIONAL TECHNOLOGY
LA English
DT Article
DE digital transformation; leadership; faculty willingness; curriculum
   innovation; advance HE framework; UAE
AB This study examines how leadership capacity drives digital transformation in higher education institutions in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), guided by the Advance HE (2025) framework for leading in higher education (HE). Using a quantitative, cross-sectional survey design supplemented by structured multiple-response items, the authors surveyed 283 academic staff and leaders and analyzed the data with partial least squares-structural equation modelling. Leadership knowledge and digital literacy, leadership values and mindsets, and institutional digital strategies and support significantly predicted faculty willingness to adopt technology. Faculty willingness mediated the association between leadership capacity and digital curriculum transformation, which in turn related to stronger student engagement and learning outcomes. Structured section 8 responses highlighted workload pressures, infrastructure constraints, and data-privacy concerns, as well as the importance of vision-led leadership and sustained institutional support. The findings suggest that sustainable digital transformation depends less on technology availability alone than on coherent leadership, faculty readiness, and curriculumcentered reform. The study offers practical implications for aligning governance, professional development, and policy in UAE HE.

TI Digital competence of Thai EFL pre-service teachers: Perceptions,
   classroom integration, and influencing factors
SO CONTEMPORARY EDUCATIONAL TECHNOLOGY
LA English
DT Article
DE teacher digital competence; EFL pre-service teachers; technology
   integration; personal-ethical competencies; personal-professional
   competencies
AB Effective digital competence and technology integration have become increasingly important for English as a foreign language (EFL) pre-service teachers (PSTs); however, they often confront various challenges, especially in the practical usage of digital technology in class. The purposes of this study were to investigate the levels of perceived digital competence of Thai EFL PSTs, to explore their digital integration in actual classroom practice, and to examine the factors contributing to their digital competence. Self-assessment questionnaires administered to 32 Thai EFL PSTs revealed a marked contrast between the highest-and lowest-rated items within the personal-ethical dimension. In classroom observations, most PSTs demonstrated a developing level of digital competence. Multimedia creation was rated at the expert level, ranking highest among the observed areas of technology integration. Lastly, the findings from semi-structured interviews revealed that supportive factors influencing their digital competence were contextual enablers, technological familiarity, personal behavior, and mentorship/peer support. In contrast, challenging factors involved institutional support, personal behaviors, insufficient digital skills, inadequate ongoing training, and difficulties in student-technology interaction. These findings emphasize the importance of a supportive school ICT culture and tiered training programs for PSTs, rangingfrom beginner to advanced levels, to promote digitally competent, confident, and innovative PSTs who are fully prepared for the dynamic demands of modern education.

AB Background Health professions educators fulfil multiple roles that are critical to effective teaching, assessment, and curriculum implementation. However, empirical evidence examining these roles across different professional fields remains limited.Aim This study aimed to explore the roles of health professions educators across professional disciplines and to examine the relationships among these roles using a validated measurement instrument.Methods A cross-sectional study design was employed using a self-administered questionnaire developed based on an integrated conceptual framework of educator roles. TI Exploring high mountain environments: high school students' perceptions
   from a place-based field trip
SO FRONTIERS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE field trip; geography education; high mountain areas; outdoor education;
   place-based education
ID CULTURAL ECOSYSTEM SERVICES; CLIMATE-CHANGE; EDUCATION; SENSE;
   ATTACHMENT; FRAMEWORK
AB Introduction In recent years, the consequences of climate change for human well-being and ecosystems have become increasingly severe. High mountain environments are undergoing changes that not only make the effects of climate change visible but generate new environmental risks. These highly dynamic environments represent powerful learning sites but also pose challenges for education due to their visible responses to rising temperatures. Place-based education offers a framework for connecting learners to meaningful real world locations, and fostering learning through direct engagement with high mountain environments. However, there is limited research on which elements of those environments support place-based learning.Methods This study aims to (1) explore how high school students perceive high mountain environments and (2) identify the environmental, social, and emotional elements that contribute to their sense of place. Adopting a multi-method approach, the high school students (n = 43; aged 14-16 years) expressed their perceptions on a field trip to the case study area, the Gaisberg Valley, Tyrol, Austria. Data were collected through focus group discussions, peer-to-peer interviews, and a photo-hike.Results The results show that the high school students hold particular interest in physical features, environmental changes related to climate change, and ecological elements. Their perceptions also revealed a strong desire to interact with the area through different perspectives, as well as emotional responses ranging from curiosity and joy to feelings of risk.Discussion Overall, the results highlight key elements of high mountain environments that can support educators in designing field trips and teaching climate change through place-based learning.

TI Student well-being, sense of belonging, and alienation among secondary
   school students in Colombia, India, and Malawi
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL DEVELOPMENT
LA English
DT Article
DE Alienation; Colombia; India; Malawi; School Climate; Sense of belonging
   and wellbeing
ID CLIMATE; CONTEXT; GIRLS; LIFE
AB Growing evidence supports the importance of students' well-being, sense of belonging, and alienation for their success in school and the labor force. Although research points to some school-related factors that influence these important outcomes, evidence from lower- and middle-income countries is limited. In this paper we report the results of a cross-country survey of over 1500 youth in urban and rural schools in Colombia, India, and Malawi. For each country we estimate ordinary least squares multiple regression models relating student well-being, sense of belonging, and alienation to school climate variables. In all three countries, we find that these three outcomes are associated significantly and in the expected direction with a range of affective experiences that teachers and school leaders can shape, including students' sense of safety and fairness in school and the quality of students' relationships with teachers, school leaders, and peers. These findings suggest that teachers, school leaders, and educational policymakers in marginalized locations can enhance students' schooling experiences by looking beyond traditional academic processes and outcomes to improve school climate.

AB In the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, many students with disabilities such as autism, mental disabilities and behavioural and emotional disorders, receive their education in general education schools. TI Teaching Challenges and Learning Gaps in First-Year University
   Accounting Course
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE Assessment Disparities; Curriculum Misalignment; Educational Policy
   Reform; Higher Education Transition; Pedagogical Challenges; Student
   Preparedness
ID FACTORS INFLUENCING SUCCESS; SOUTH-AFRICAN UNIVERSITY;
   ACADEMIC-PERFORMANCE; STUDENTS; KNOWLEDGE; EDUCATION; IMPACT
AB The transition from high school to university accounting education poses significant challenges for students and lecturers. This study examines the gaps between high school and first-year university accounting education in South Africa and explores the challenges lecturers encounter when teaching first-year students. The research adopted a qualitative design to gain in-depth insights into these issues. Data were collected through semi structured interviews and focus group discussions with six accounting lecturers and twelve first-year students. Responses were transcribed, coded, and analysed thematically using ATLAS.ti software. Findings indicate significant curriculum misalignment between high school and university accounting programs, resulting in inadequate student preparedness and difficulties in applying theoretical knowledge to practical scenarios. Lecturers reported challenges such as insufficient teaching time, diverse student backgrounds, and negative learning attitudes. The study concludes that bridging programs, curriculum updates, and improved instructional strategies are essential to enhance student readiness and support successful transitions to university-level accounting education.

TI Regional Language Instruction in Jharkhand, India
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE Academic Achievement; Language Proficiency; Primary Grades; Regional
   Language; Socioeconomic Factors
AB This study investigates the effect of regional language Nagpuri instruction levels on academic achievement in 412 participants from primary grades of 10 government schools in the state of Jharkhand, India. Using quantitative methods, the research analyses academic achievement scores across three instructional levels (low, medium, high) and correlates them with language proficiency and socioeconomic status. Results from t-tests and ANOVA reveal significant differences in mean scores between instructional levels, with higher proficiency associated with higher academic achievement. A strong positive correlation (r = 0.62, p < 0.001) between academic achievement and language proficiency underscores the importance of language skills in educational outcomes. Regression analysis confirms language proficiency as a significant predictor (<(a)over bar> = 0.81, p < 0.001), even when controlling for socioeconomic factors (<(a)over bar> = 0.26, p = 0.001). Findings suggest that incorporating regional language instruction could potentially narrow achievement gaps and improve educational equity.

TI Pedagogy in a State College During Educational Disruption: A Strategic
   Framework for Sustainable Teacher Development
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE Flexible Pedagogy; Teacher Development; TOWS Matrix; Sustainable
   Instruction; Opportunities
AB This study evaluated the implementation of flexible pedagogy in a state college and developed a Sustainable Teacher Development Program (STDP) to strengthen instructional adaptability and long-term faculty growth. Descriptive multi-methods design was used, data were gathered from faculty who implemented flexible teaching between 2020 and 2022 through a validated survey measuring pedagogical practices and a qualitative component based on SWOT analysis. Results revealed strong institutional and instructional capacities, including effective technology integration, diverse learning resources, and robust academic support. However, weaknesses such as limited learner autonomy, inconsistent differentiated instruction, and gaps in ICT and psychosocial support persist. Opportunities in professional development, resource-sharing platforms, and technological innovations are present while threats-connectivity issues, workload pressures, infrastructure limitations, and resistance to change, which pose ongoing challenges. Through the TOWS matrix, strategic orientations were formulated and integrated into the STDP S-Framework (Stability, Skill-Building, Systems, Support, Sustainability), which sustains flexible pedagogy of teachers.

TI Accessibility and Equity in Online Learning for Deaf and Hard of Hearing
   Students in Saudi Arabia
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE Assistive Technology; Digital Inclusion; Higher Education; Mixed
   Methods; Universal Design
AB This empirical study examines accessibility and equity in online learning for Deaf and Hard of Hearing (DHH) students in Saudi Arabia, where digital education has rapidly expanded under Vision 2030. Despite advances in assistive technologies, many DHH learners continue to face systemic barriers related to captioning, sign-language interpretation, platform design, and instructor preparedness. Using a mixed-method design, data were collected from 52 DHH university students and 15 online-learning instructors across three Saudi public universities. Participants were selected using purposive sampling from disability support centers in Saudi Arabia. Quantitative data were analysed descriptively to measure accessibility frequency, perceived inclusion, and satisfaction, while qualitative interviews explored lived experiences and institutional support. Results revealed that although 68 percent of DHH participants accessed online classes weekly, only 41 percent reported reliable captioning, and 56 percent experienced communication delays with instructors. Qualitative findings indicated that institutional awareness and staff training strongly predicted students' sense of inclusion.

TI Scientific Trends of Large Language Model Assisted Pedagogy in Higher
   Education: A Bibliometric Analysis
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE Collaboration; Co-Occurrence; Journal; Network; VOSviewer
AB This research work presents a bibliometric analysis of Large Language Model (LMM)-assisted pedagogy in higher education to study its global research trends and identify key themes, collaboration patterns, and research gaps. Lens (Lens.org) was used to retrieve the dataset by incorporating a logical and expanded structure from December 2015 to December 2025. A total of 17,089 relevant records were retrieved and analysed. VOSviewer was used for keyword co-occurrence, author collaboration, and journal-source network analyses. The results showed that LLM-assisted pedagogy research surged between 2020 and 2022. It can be concluded that the findings may play a pivotal role in policy framing in LLM-assisted pedagogy development in higher education.

TI Hybrid-Flexible (Hyflex) Classroom Management Framework: A Case in One
   State College in Camarines Sur, Philippines
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE Classroom Instruction; Education; Pedagogy; Proposed Framework; Virtual
   Classroom
AB The COVID-19 pandemic has compelled educational institutions to adopt online instead of traditional classroom instruction as the new norm in education. The study aimed to develop a hybrid-flexible (HyFlex) classroom management framework from one state college in Camarines Sur. The study employed the sequential explanatory strategy under the mixed methods with 191 respondents obtained using Slovin's formula. Setting time allocation of activities of the class, sequencing and integrating additional activities, reinforcing good classroom behaviour, and sustaining an open communication channel, and giving high regard to right conduct and attitudes was mostly practiced and there is no significant difference between these practices. The HyFlex classroom management framework was developed as a springboard for other institutions to craft their own framework for new normal education. However, further validation of the framework is suggested. The developed framework may serve as a basis for the upskilling and retooling of faculty within and outside the institution.

TI Future Prospects of Agripreneurship: A Study on Career Aspirations of
   State Agricultural University Students in Gujarat
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE Agripreneurship; Aspiration; Education; Employment. Gujarat; Gujarat;
   Students
AB This study examined the career aspirations of agricultural students and identified key personal, psychological and informational factors influencing them. Data were collected from undergraduate, postgraduate and Ph.D. students from State Agricultural Universities in Gujarat using a structured interview schedule, and weighted mean scores and Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) were applied for analysis. Results indicated a strong preference for secure and prestigious careers, particularly government jobs such as administrative services, nationalised banks, and UPSC positions, while private and NGO employment was less preferred due to perceived instability. TI Teacher Judgment of English Language Competency and Students'
   Personality Factors: A Descriptive Study
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE Gender; Personality; Similarity; Socioeconomic; Status; Teacher Bias
ID ACCURACY; SIMILARITY; EDUCATION
AB Teacher judgment is a cognitive and social process that has received limited attention in educational research. The objective of the present study is to examine the effect of personality similarity on teachers' judgment of students' English language competence. The cross-sectional survey design has been selected in the descriptive study. The sample has been drawn from public elementary schools and comprised 97 English language teachers and their 456 students. Multiple regression analysis has been performed to analyse the effect of personality similarity, socioeconomic status, and gender on teacher judgment. It has been found that personality similarity, socioeconomic status, and gender significantly predict teachers' judgment. It can be concluded that teachers judged students positively who exhibited a high personality similarity with them. The awareness among the teachers to create inclusive learning environments and mitigate judgment bias should be developed by teacher training programs.

TI The Importance of the Mother Tongue in Education for Academic Success:
   Switzerland Basel Native Language and Culture Lessons (HSK)
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF INSTRUCTION
LA English
DT Article
DE native language; culture lessons (HSK); mother tongue; cultural
   education; academic success; Switzerland; Basel; education
AB A native language, also known as a first language or mother tongue, is the language a person is exposed to from birth or during early childhood. Learning one's native language greatly supports the acquisition of a second language. Furthermore, students who continue to develop their native language skills tend to achieve higher academic success in later years. Speaking multiple languages offers many advantages. Those who understand cultural differences have an easier time in our society. Native language and culture lessons (HSK) teach your child the language and culture of their home country. Children explore history, geography, civics, food, festivals, and customs. Highly qualified HSK teachers lead the courses with great dedication. The lessons follow the curricula and guidelines of the respective countries. Native language and culture instruction is available in approximately 40 languages in Basel-Stadt. The lessons are offered weekly in state schools and consist of two or three sessions. Children attend a session as close as possible to their homes. The lessons take place outside of normal school hours, such as on Wednesday afternoons when there is no school or on Saturday mornings. In HSK classes, children and teenagers from different schools but the same grade level are taught together. In some classes, younger and older children also learn together. Depending on the language, your child can attend classes as early as kindergarten; some courses begin in the first year of primary school. Your child can usually attend HSK classes until the end of their schooling. HSK instruction is an important component in the language development of bilingual and multilingual students and makes a significant contribution to their integration. By engaging with cultural and social issues or exploring specific topics related to nature, humanity, and society, as outlined in the mandatory HSK curriculum framework, students become aware of both the differences and similarities compared to Switzerland and reflect on their own actions and thoughts. This increases their chances of successful integration. More detailed information can be found at https://www.bs.ch/ed/volksschulen/hsk.
